title: A febrile infant 8 to 21 days old is admitted
lead: A well-appearing infant 8 to 21 days old with a fever of 38.0°C or higher gets urine, blood, and cerebrospinal fluid cultures and parenteral antibiotics in the hospital.
lines: This is not an outpatient viral visit.
The AAP 2021 guideline is the source of that age band.
Do not subtract the rectal temperature because the baby looks calm.
miss: Sending a 2-week-old with a fever of 38.2 home with a virus explanation.
diagramAlt: Fever, age 8 to 21 days. 38.0°C or higher Urine, blood, and CSF cultures Admit. Parenteral antibiotics

source.name: AAP Clinical Practice Guideline. Evaluation and Management of Well-Appearing Febrile Infants 8 to 60 Days Old.
source.says: This guideline addresses the evaluation and management of well-appearing, term infants, 8 to 60 days of age, with fever ≥38.0°C. Three algorithms summarize the recommendations for infants 8 to 21 days of age, 22 to 28 days of age, and 29 to 60 days of age.

title: A newborn of a mother with diabetes is fed and the glucose is checked
lead: A newborn whose mother had diabetes is fed early and the glucose is checked. The baby's insulin is still high after the cord is cut.
lines: Jitteriness is a low glucose until proved otherwise.
Do not wait for a seizure to check.
Feed in the first hour. Maternal glucose is gone and fetal insulin is still high, so the glucose can fall.
miss: Discharging a jittery infant of a diabetic mother at 6 hours without a glucose.

source.name: AAP Clinical Report. Postnatal Glucose Homeostasis in Late-Preterm and Term Infants.
source.says: Current evidence does not support a specific glucose concentration that discriminates normal from abnormal. Early identification of the at-risk infant and institution of prophylactic measures to prevent neonatal hypoglycemia are recommended as a pragmatic approach.

title: A Turner girl's blood pressure is measured in the arm and the leg
lead: At every visit for Turner syndrome, compare the arm and the leg blood pressure and listen for the aortic valve. The karyotype result is not a completed plan.
lines: A new gradient is imaging, not a year of observation.
Growth hormone and estrogen are timed with a specialist, not started casually.
Renal ultrasound is done if it was never done.
miss: Refilling a note that says Turner and never taking a leg pressure.

source.name: Clinical practice guidelines for the care of girls and women with Turner syndrome.
source.says: R 4.5: where postnatal TTE is not available, clinical cardiac evaluation with 4-extremity blood pressure, pulse oximetry, palpation of femoral pulses, cardiac auscultation, and ECG before discharge. R 4.17: annual assessment of blood pressure for all individuals with TS. R 7.21: a renal ultrasound at time of diagnosis.

title: Salt-wasting adrenal crisis in an infant is steroid and saline first
lead: A vomiting, shocked infant in the first weeks of life gets a glucose, a sodium, a potassium, and a stress-dose steroid. The genital exam does not delay the steroid.
lines: A virilized or atypical newborn is evaluated for 21-hydroxylase deficiency before anyone assigns a sex or sends the infant home.
The infant who is ill is treated, not observed until a karyotype result returns.
In weeks 1 to 3 the sodium falls and the potassium rises, often above 6. 17-hydroxyprogesterone is very high. Give hydrocortisone and saline, then fludrocortisone.
miss: Discharging a virilized newborn with no plan for salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency.
diagramAlt: Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase. Week 1–3: Na low, K over 6 17-hydroxyprogesterone very high Hydrocortisone + saline, then fludrocortisone

source.name: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia Due to Steroid 21-Hydroxylase Deficiency.
source.says: Missed diagnosis of salt-losing CAH is associated with increased risk for early neonatal morbidity and mortality. 4.3 In the newborn and in early infancy, we recommend using fludrocortisone and sodium chloride supplements to the treatment regimen.

title: The first sickle-cell pain order is incentive spirometry
lead: For a sickle-cell pain crisis, write incentive spirometry on admission. It prevents acute chest syndrome while you treat the pain.
lines: Oxygen is for hypoxia, not for a saturation of 99%.
Fluids are enough to correct deficit, not a flood.
Incentive spirometry on every pain admission. A new infiltrate plus hypoxia is acute chest syndrome.
Exchange transfusion for severe acute chest or acute stroke. Simple transfusion is for symptomatic anemia. Hydroxyurea is prevention, not today's stroke drug.
miss: Admitting for morphine without a spirometer or a plan to walk.

source.name: NHLBI Expert Panel Report. Evidence-Based Management of Sickle Cell Disease.
source.says: To reduce the risk of acute chest syndrome in adults and children hospitalized for a VOC, encourage use of incentive spirometry while awake. Perform urgent exchange transfusion when there is rapid progression of ACS, such as oxygen saturation below 90 percent despite supplemental oxygen.

more.name: BSH guideline on acute chest syndrome in sickle cell disease (2015).

title: Exchange transfusion is the order for severe acute chest or stroke
lead: Severe acute chest syndrome or an acute stroke in sickle cell disease is an exchange-transfusion call, not another unit of simple transfusion as the whole plan.
lines: Simple transfusion is for symptomatic anemia.
Call the blood bank early. The exchange takes time to arrange.
Hydroxyurea is the outpatient prevention, not the drug that treats today's stroke.
Incentive spirometry on every pain admission. A new infiltrate plus hypoxia is acute chest syndrome.
miss: Ordering one unit of packed cells and a neurology clinic visit for an acute ischemic stroke in sickle cell disease.

source.name: American Society of Hematology 2020 guidelines for sickle cell disease: prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cerebrovascular disease.
source.says: Recommendation 4.1: for acute neurological deficits including TIA, prompt blood transfusion, given without delay beyond 2 hours. Recommendation 4.2: exchange transfusion is suggested over simple transfusion. NHLBI 2014: urgent exchange transfusion for rapidly progressing acute chest syndrome.

more.name: NHLBI Expert Panel Report. Evidence-Based Management of Sickle Cell Disease (2014): urgent exchange transfusion for rapidly progressing acute chest syndrome; simple transfusion for symptomatic anemia.

title: Plasma exchange is ordered before the ADAMTS13 returns
lead: When the smear and the story are thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, order plasma exchange now. The ADAMTS13 result confirms later.
lines: High clinical suspicion: draw ADAMTS13 before any plasma exchange or blood product.
Then start therapeutic plasma exchange and corticosteroids without waiting for the ADAMTS13 result.
The ISTH treatment guideline strongly recommends adding corticosteroids to plasma exchange for a first episode or a relapse.
Caplacizumab is a conditional addition in the treatment guideline. It is not a reason to delay plasma exchange.
miss: Waiting for the ADAMTS13 result before plasma exchange when the clinical suspicion is already high.
diagramAlt: TTP versus ITP. TTP: schistocytes, hemolysis, exchange now ITP: isolated low platelets, no fragments Platelets in TTP only for life-threatening bleed

source.name: ISTH guidelines for the diagnosis of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.
source.says: If the pretest probability of TTP is high, start TPE and corticosteroids, and collect plasma samples for ADAMTS13 testing before therapy. Acquire a plasma sample for ADAMTS13 testing before an initiation of TPE or use of any blood product.

title: Febrile neutropenia is treated with broad antibiotics immediately
lead: Write the antipseudomonal antibiotic as a stat order. Add vancomycin only for instability, a line infection, severe mucositis, or known resistant gram-positive colonization.
lines: Fever plus neutropenia is treated at once with broad empiric antibiotics. Do not wait for a culture to grow.
Risk stratification decides the setting. It does not delay the first dose.
A narrow oral drug chosen before that first broad dose is the miss.
miss: Waiting for the culture result before the first broad antibiotic dose.

source.name: IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline for the Use of Antimicrobial Agents in Neutropenic Patients With Cancer: 2010 Update.
source.says: What has not changed is the indication for immediate empirical antibiotic therapy. It remains true that all patients who present with fever and neutropenia should be treated swiftly and broadly with antibiotics to treat both gram-positive and gram-negative pathogens.

more.name: ASCO/IDSA 2018 update. Outpatient Management of Fever and Neutropenia (antipseudomonal beta-lactam monotherapy within 1 hour).

title: A head bleed in hemophilia is factor first, scan second
lead: A hemophilia patient with head trauma gets factor replacement immediately. The CT does not come before the factor.
lines: Aim for a full correction for a central-nervous-system bleed.
An inhibitor is suspected when the bleed does not stop with the usual dose.
PT is normal. PTT is long and corrects with mixing unless an inhibitor has formed.
miss: Sending the patient to CT while the factor is still in the pharmacy.

source.name: WFH Guidelines for the Management of Hemophilia, 3rd edition.
source.says: In the event of significant head trauma or clinical suspicion of central nervous system and/or intracranial hemorrhage, immediate treatment with CFC infusion is required without waiting for further symptoms to develop or for laboratory or radiologic evaluation.

more.name: StatPearls. Hemophilia A (mixing study, inhibitors).

title: Stop heparin in all its forms when HIT is suspected
lead: When heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is suspected, discontinue every heparin product, including flushes and coated catheters, and order a non-heparin anticoagulant.
lines: Estimate probability with the 4Ts score, not a gestalt impression.
A low-probability 4Ts score is not an indication to stop heparin and start another anticoagulant.
An intermediate or high score: stop heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant. ASH names argatroban, bivalirudin, danaparoid, fondaparinux, and a direct oral anticoagulant.
Do not start warfarin before the platelet count recovers, usually to at least 150 × 10^9/L. Early warfarin is linked to venous limb gangrene.
miss: Stopping heparin without a non-heparin anticoagulant when the 4Ts score is intermediate or high, or starting warfarin while the platelet count is still low.
diagramAlt: HIT, day 5 to 10. Platelets fall >=50% at day 5-10 With or without thrombosis Stop heparin. No warfarin before recovery

source.name: ASH 2018 guidelines for management of venous thromboembolism: heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
source.says: Strong recommendations include use of the 4Ts score rather than a gestalt approach and avoidance of empiric treatment of HIT with a low-probability 4Ts score. The panel suggests argatroban, bivalirudin, danaparoid, fondaparinux, or a DOAC, and recommends against a VKA before platelet count recovery (usually ≥150 × 10^9/L).

title: Cryoprecipitate is the fibrinogen order in DIC
lead: In a bleeding patient with DIC and a low fibrinogen, order cryoprecipitate. Ordering only fresh frozen plasma does not reliably replace fibrinogen.
lines: Treat the cause. That remains the first DIC order.
If the patient is bleeding and fibrinogen is under 1.5 g/L, give cryoprecipitate.
Platelets or plasma are for bleeding, not for a daily laboratory target.
Therapeutic heparin is for a thrombotic picture, not for a patient who is already bleeding.
miss: Replacing volume with plasma alone while fibrinogen stays under 1.5 g/L in a bleeding patient.
diagramAlt: DIC labs. Low fibrinogen, high D-dimer PT and PTT both prolong Cryoprecipitate if bleeding and fibrinogen is low

source.name: ISTH SSC guidance. Diagnosis and treatment of DIC, harmonized from three guidelines.
source.says: The cornerstone of DIC treatment is the treatment of the underlying condition. In general, transfusion of platelets or plasma (components) in patients with DIC should be reserved for patients who are bleeding. Prophylactic doses of unfractionated heparin or low molecular weight heparin is recommended in critically ill and non-bleeding patients with DIC.

title: Rasburicase is a stat order, and the uric acid tube is special
lead: If you give rasburicase, the uric-acid sample has to be handled so the drug does not keep working in the tube and fake a low result.
lines: Fluids are already running.
The potassium is on a monitor and a repeat lab.
G6PD deficiency is the contraindication you ask about.
Potassium and phosphate and uric acid rise. Calcium falls.
Allopurinol stops new uric acid formation. Rasburicase destroys uric acid already present.
miss: Celebrating a uric acid of 1 drawn in a warm tube after rasburicase.
diagramAlt: Tumor lysis ions. K up, phosphate up, uric acid up Calcium down (binds phosphate) Rasburicase clears uric acid already made

source.name: British Society for Haematology updated guidelines for the diagnosis and management of tumour lysis syndrome in adults and children with haematological malignancies.
source.says: Patients with established TLS should be treated with rasburicase 0.2 mg/kg/day. Allopurinol should be stopped when rasburicase is commenced. Patients who may receive rasburicase should be tested for G6PD deficiency, as rasburicase can cause haemolytic anaemia or methaemoglobinaemia. Patients with TLS should have vigorous intravenous hydration.

title: Phlebotomy for polycythemia vera has a hematocrit target
lead: Order phlebotomy for polycythemia vera toward a hematocrit under 45%, and do not apply that target to a hypoxic patient with a high erythropoietin.
lines: Aspirin is added when the diagnosis is secure.
Hydroxyurea is for the high-risk patient, written as a planned drug, not a one-time dose.
Tell the patient to report erythromelalgia and clots.
A high EPO is secondary erythrocytosis.
miss: Phlebotomizing a patient with COPD and a high EPO down to a hematocrit of 40.
diagramAlt: Polycythemia vera target. JAK2. EPO is low Phlebotomy toward hematocrit <45% Do not phlebotomize hypoxic high-EPO disease

source.name: ELN revised management recommendations for Philadelphia chromosome-negative classical myeloproliferative neoplasms.
source.says: The Panel strongly recommended that all patients with PV should be managed with phlebotomy to maintain the hematocrit below 45%, together with daily low-dose acetyl salicylic acid.

title: ATRA is a now order, and the fibrinogen is checked twice a shift
lead: For suspected acute promyelocytic leukemia, order all-trans retinoic acid and a fibrinogen now, and recheck the fibrinogen on the same shift.
lines: The blood bank knows this patient can bleed.
Differentiation syndrome is fever and infiltrates after the drug. Do not call it pneumonia and stop the drug without a specialist.
The genetic test is sent. It is not the start time.
Start all-trans retinoic acid when the smear fits. Do not wait for the karyotype. Recheck fibrinogen the same day.
miss: Scheduling the bone-marrow biopsy for Monday and the drug for after the result.
diagramAlt: APL, do not wait. Auer rods. t(15;17) ATRA when the smear fits Bleeding is the early death. Follow fibrinogen

source.name: ELN expert-panel recommendations for the management of acute promyelocytic leukemia.
source.says: ATRA should be initiated immediately once APL is suspected. Transfusions of fibrinogen and/or cryoprecipitate, platelets, and fresh-frozen plasma should be given to maintain the fibrinogen concentration above 100 to 150 mg/dL and the platelet count above 30 to 50 × 10^9/L.

title: Vaccinate before or as you start a complement inhibitor
lead: Before or as a complement inhibitor starts for PNH, order meningococcal vaccination. The drug blocks the defense against Neisseria.
lines: The hemolysis drug is not delayed for a life-threatening clot, and the vaccine is not forgotten.
Iron is replaced if the urine has been losing it.
Anticoagulation alone is not the whole plan.
miss: Starting eculizumab on Friday and leaving the vaccine for a clinic that does not exist.

source.name: Meningococcal Vaccination: Recommendations of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, United States, 2020.
source.says: MenACWY and MenB are recommended for persons receiving a complement inhibitor (e.g., eculizumab or ravulizumab). Persons using complement inhibitor should be vaccinated at least 2 weeks before complement inhibitor initiation unless the risks for delaying treatment outweigh the risks for developing meningococcal disease.

title: A transfusion reaction order is stop, keep, and send
lead: The order set for a suspected hemolytic reaction is: stop the transfusion, keep the bag and tubing, send a new sample, and do not restart that unit.
lines: Normal saline is the fluid. More blood is a new decision.
Check the name on the bag against the wristband yourself.
Urine output and pressure are the bedside monitors.
ABO mismatch causes fever, flank pain, and hemoglobinuria during the transfusion. Stop that unit.
Keep the bag. Send it back with a fresh sample. Clerical error is the usual cause. Do not restart the same unit.
miss: Slowing the rate to 10 mL an hour and leaving the same unit hanging.

source.name: BSH Guideline on the investigation and management of acute transfusion reactions.
source.says: If a patient develops new symptoms or signs during a transfusion, this should be stopped temporarily but venous access should be maintained, and identification details checked against the component. If febrile symptoms are sustained, a haemolytic reaction should be considered, the unit returned, and samples taken for repeat compatibility testing.

more.name: StatPearls. Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction.

title: Myeloma is plasma cells and end-organ damage
lead: Multiple myeloma is abnormal plasma cells in the marrow that cause end-organ damage. Most patients who respond later relapse.
lines: It is a B-cell disorder of monoclonal plasma cells, in the marrow or outside it.
End-organ damage is part of the disease, not a separate illness.
Primary refractory disease never reaches even a minimal response on the first treatment.
Relapse after a remission is the common later course.
miss: Treating a plasma-cell cancer as cured because the first response looked complete.

source.name: StatPearls. Multiple Myeloma.
source.says: Multiple myeloma is a clonal plasma cell proliferative disorder characterized by the abnormal increase of monoclonal paraprotein leading to evidence of specific end-organ damage. Most commonly this is hypercalcemia, renal dysfunction, anemia, or bone pain with lytic lesions.

title: Aplastic anemia transfusions are limited if transplant is possible
lead: In a young patient with aplastic anemia who may be transplanted, transfuse for symptoms and avoid blood from family donors, who can sensitize the recipient.
lines: The marrow is the diagnostic test and is ordered, not inferred.
Infection precautions are written.
Growth factors are not a substitute for a diagnosis.
Reticulocytes are low and the marrow is empty. Splenomegaly argues against aplastic anemia.
miss: Transfusing a sibling's directed donation the night before a transplant evaluation.

source.name: StatPearls. Aplastic Anemia.
source.says: Patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA) or very severe aplastic anemia (vSAA) require prompt treatment to reduce the risk of life-threatening infections and limit complications from ongoing transfusions and medications.

title: Blood pressure before a thrombolytic is under 185/110
lead: Before alteplase or tenecteplase, the blood pressure is brought under 185/110. If you are not giving a reperfusion drug and the pressure is under 220/120, do not lower it in the first two days.
lines: Write the thrombolytic only after the pressure is in range and the exclusion list is checked.
A patient who is not reperfused is harmed by an aggressive pressure drop.
Recheck the pressure after the drug. The target while the infusion's risk window is open is lower still, under about 180/105.
miss: Lowering a pressure of 190/100 in a patient who is not getting a thrombolytic, or giving the drug at 200/115.
diagramAlt: Thrombolysis inside 4.5 hours. Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg max 25 mg, or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg max 90 mg. Pressure under 185/110 first.

source.name: 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke.
source.says: The guideline endorses either alteplase or tenecteplase in the 4.5-hour window: tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg); a 0.4 mg/kg tenecteplase dose is not recommended. Disabling deficits are treated regardless of NIHSS score, without advanced imaging selection; BP is brought below 185/110 first.

title: The stroke order is a finger-stick and a CT before the drug
lead: The first stroke orders are a glucose, a noncontrast CT, and a clock. Hypoglycemia copies a stroke and is treated, not lysed.
lines: The CT excludes hemorrhage. It does not have to show the infarct.
A swallow screen is ordered before the first meal.
Glucose and noncontrast CT precede thrombolysis. MRI is not required inside the standard window.
Inside 4.5 hours, tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (maximum 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (maximum 90 mg). Blood pressure before the drug is under 185/110. The 0.4 mg/kg tenecteplase dose is not the one used.
miss: Sending the patient to MRI and giving breakfast before a swallow screen.
diagramAlt: Thrombolysis inside 4.5 hours. Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg max 25 mg, or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg max 90 mg. Pressure under 185/110 first.

source.name: 2026 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke.
source.says: The guideline endorses either alteplase or tenecteplase in the 4.5-hour window: tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg) or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg); a 0.4 mg/kg tenecteplase dose is not recommended. Disabling deficits are treated regardless of NIHSS score, without advanced imaging selection; BP is brought below 185/110 first.

title: Status epilepticus orders: glucose, benzo, then one full second drug
lead: The status order is a glucose, a benzodiazepine now, and if it continues one full dose of levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, or valproate.
lines: Do not stack quarter-doses of lorazepam.
Protect the airway while the drugs are drawn.
A benzodiazepine level or a neurology consult is not the first order.
Check glucose, then give a benzodiazepine: intravenous lorazepam or intramuscular midazolam if there is no line.

If the seizure continues, give one full dose of levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4500 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg/kg (max 1500 mg), or valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3000 mg). ESETT found them equivalent. Do not stack quarter-doses.
miss: Starting a phenytoin load and never giving the benzodiazepine.
diagramAlt: Status epilepticus drugs. Glucose, then a benzodiazepine Then one full second drug Levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, or valproate

source.name: AES Evidence-Based Guideline: Treatment of Convulsive Status Epilepticus in Children and Adults.
source.says: A benzodiazepine (specifically IM midazolam, IV lorazepam, or IV diazepam) is recommended as the initial therapy of choice (level A). Compared to the first therapy, the second therapy is less effective (level A).

more.name: ESETT (Kapur, NEJM 2019): levetiracetam 60 mg/kg (max 4500 mg), fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg (max 1500), valproate 40 mg/kg (max 3000) after benzodiazepines; similar efficacy.

title: A thunderclap order is CT now, and a plan if it is negative
lead: Order a noncontrast head CT before any migraine drug for a headache that peaked at onset. If it is negative in the first hours, order the next test rather than a discharge.
lines: The next test is a lumbar puncture or a vascular study, chosen by timing.
Do not give a triptan to a headache you have not cleared.
Document the time the pain became maximal.
Maximal at onset means noncontrast CT before any migraine drug.
miss: Discharging a negative CT at hour two with a sumatriptan prescription.

source.name: 2023 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
source.says: Noncontrast head CT remains the mainstay of SAH diagnosis. For patients presenting within 6 hours of headache onset who have no new neurological deficits, the lack of SAH on a noncontrast head CT is likely sufficient to exclude aSAH; otherwise LP for xanthochromia or CTA is the next study after a negative or nondiagnostic CT.

title: Meningitis: steroid and drug before the scanner if you must scan
lead: If a CT is required before the lumbar puncture, the dexamethasone and the antibiotic are given first. The puncture happens after the scan.
lines: Blood cultures are drawn if they do not delay the drug.
The steroid is with the first dose when pneumococcus is likely.
A normal CT does not mean you skip the puncture.
Dexamethasone is given before or with the first dose when adult pneumococcal meningitis is suspected. A normal CT does not cancel the puncture.
miss: Holding the antibiotic until the patient returns from CT and the puncture is done.
diagramAlt: Adult bacterial meningitis. Dexamethasone before or with dose 1 If CT is required, drug still goes in first Stop steroid if pneumococcus is excluded

source.name: NICE guideline NG240. Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management.
source.says: Antibiotics start within 1 hour of arrival; blood tests and lumbar puncture are performed before antibiotics only if safe and without clinically significant delay. Give dexamethasone with or before the first antibiotic dose if possible.

more.name: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Management of Bacterial Meningitis (2004, archived).

title: Watch the numbers that say the diaphragm is failing
lead: In Guillain-Barré syndrome, order vital capacity and negative inspiratory force on a schedule. Intubate when those numbers fall, not when the patient arrests.
lines: IVIg 0.4 g/kg daily for 5 days if the patient cannot walk unaided and weakness began within 2 weeks. A good-practice point also allows 2 to 4 weeks.
Or plasma exchange, 12–15 L in four to five exchanges over 1 to 2 weeks, if weakness began within 4 weeks and the patient cannot walk unaided.
Do not use oral corticosteroids. A second course of IVIg for a poor prognosis is recommended against.
Use the modified Erasmus GBS Respiratory Insufficiency Score for the ventilation risk. CSF examination is valuable when the diagnosis is uncertain.
miss: Starting prednisone, or quoting a vital-capacity cutoff this guideline does not use, instead of IVIg or plasma exchange.
diagramAlt: Guillain-Barré breathing. IVIG or exchange. Not prednisone Vital capacity under 20 mL/kg: intubate window CSF: high protein, almost no cells

source.name: EAN/PNS guideline on diagnosis and treatment of Guillain-Barré syndrome.
source.says: The task force recommends IVIg 0.4 g/kg for 5 days within 2 weeks (GPP also within 2-4 weeks) after onset of weakness if unable to walk unaided, or plasma exchange 12-15 L in four to five exchanges over 1-2 weeks within 4 weeks; it recommends against oral corticosteroids and advises the mEGRIS score for ventilation risk.

title: A multiple-sclerosis admission includes a search for infection
lead: Before you order a high-dose steroid for a supposed flare, order a search for infection. A urinary infection can revive old symptoms.
lines: The AAN guideline recommends offering a disease-modifying therapy for relapsing multiple sclerosis.
Reconcile that drug at discharge so a dose is not missed.
Old weakness plus a fever is not automatically a new lesion. Look for infection before you escalate therapy.
MRI is for a new deficit, not for every warm afternoon.
miss: Starting high-dose steroids for a urinary infection and yesterday's deficit.
diagramAlt: MS flare versus infection. New deficit: high-dose steroid Old deficit plus fever: find the infection Disease-modifying drug is a separate order

source.name: NICE guideline NG220. Multiple sclerosis in adults: management.
source.says: Explain to people with MS that the possible causes of symptom changes include another illness such as an infection, further relapse, or change of disease status. Not all relapses need treating with steroids.

more.name: AAN practice guideline. Disease-modifying therapies for adults with multiple sclerosis (2018).

title: Parkinson medications are given on the patient's clock
lead: In the hospital, order carbidopa-levodopa at the patient's home times. A missed dose causes rigidity that looks like a new illness.
lines: Do not order a dopamine blocker for nausea.
A swallowing evaluation is ordered if the doses are being missed because of dysphagia.
Fall precautions are written.
Rest tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia from nigral dopamine loss. Give hospital doses at the home clock times.
Metoclopramide and haloperidol block dopamine and copy the disease. Levodopa is the most effective motor drug.
miss: Holding all Parkinson drugs because the patient is NPO for a test that could have been timed.
diagramAlt: Parkinson doses in hospital. Give carbidopa-levodopa at home times No metoclopramide or haloperidol Levodopa is the strongest motor drug

source.name: StatPearls. Parkinson Disease.
source.says: Oral levodopa is the most effective treatment for the motor symptoms of PD. Levodopa, absorbed from the gut, is converted to dopamine; carbidopa, a dopa decarboxylase inhibitor, is co-administered.

title: Cord compression: dexamethasone and MRI today
lead: Order dexamethasone and an MRI today for back pain with leg weakness, a sensory level, or new urinary retention. The oncology staging can wait.
lines: Radiation oncology or spine surgery is called when the MRI confirms compression.
Plain films are not the test.
A bladder scan documents the retention.
Suspected metastatic spinal cord compression is treated with corticosteroids and urgent MRI, not with plain films as the clearance test.
miss: Scheduling the MRI for next week and a clinic visit.
diagramAlt: Cord compression. Dexamethasone immediately MRI today, not plain films Decompress. Do not wait for full staging

source.name: NICE NG234. Spinal metastases and metastatic spinal cord compression.
source.says: Offer MRI to people with suspected MSCC and do not use plain X-ray of the spine to diagnose or rule it out. Offer 16 mg of oral dexamethasone as soon as possible and continue it daily while awaiting surgery or radiotherapy.

title: A TIA leaves with a drug and a monitored plan
lead: A TIA discharge order includes an antithrombotic, a statin if atherosclerotic disease is the cause, and a follow-up measured in days, not months.
lines: If atrial fibrillation is found, the drug is an anticoagulant, not aspirin.
Carotid imaging is ordered before or immediately after discharge.
Driving and the next symptom are written in the instructions.
miss: Discharging on aspirin with a neurology appointment in three months and no carotid study.
diagramAlt: TIA before discharge. Antithrombotic today AF found: anticoagulant, not aspirin Carotid imaging, not a visit in 3 months

source.name: 2021 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack.
source.says: Diagnostic tests for the cause of a TIA should be completed within 48 hours when possible. Prescribe antithrombotic therapy; screen for atrial fibrillation and anticoagulate if found; consider endarterectomy or stenting for severe ipsilateral carotid stenosis.

title: Horner syndrome imaging is ordered the day you see it
lead: Order vascular imaging the day you diagnose a painful Horner syndrome. A chest image that includes the apex is added for a smoker.
lines: Do not schedule it as a routine outpatient study next month.
Neurologic signs beyond the eye move the patient to a stroke pathway.
Document which pupil is small.
Ptosis and miosis from lost sympathetics. A third-nerve palsy is a down-and-out eye with a blown pupil.
Painful acute Horner syndrome is carotid dissection until the vessel is imaged the same day.
miss: Referring to ophthalmology in two weeks for a painful drooping lid.

source.name: ACR Appropriateness Criteria. Horner Syndrome.
source.says: For acute painful Horner syndrome, and for nonacute nonlocalizable Horner syndrome, CTA head and neck with IV contrast is rated usually appropriate as initial imaging.

title: Medication-overuse headache is counted in days per month
lead: A migraine discharge names the acute drug, the limit per week, and the red flags that mean come back. Daily painkillers create the next headache.
lines: Headache on 15 or more days a month, for more than 3 months, in someone with a prior headache disorder, is the ICHD-3 frame for medication-overuse headache.
Triptans, ergots, opioids, and combination analgesics meet overuse at 10 or more days a month.
The treatment implied by the diagnosis is to stop the overused acute drug, not to raise the monthly count.
miss: Refilling a near-daily triptan or combination analgesic without counting the days per month.

source.name: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (ICHD-3). 8.2.2 Triptan-overuse headache.
source.says: Triptan-overuse headache is headache occurring on 15 or more days/month in a patient with a pre-existing primary headache, developing as a consequence of regular use of one or more triptans on 10 or more days/month for more than 3 months.

title: Delirium orders remove the cause and the anticholinergic
lead: The delirium order set looks for infection, drugs, urine retention, and constipation, and it stops diphenhydramine. A benzodiazepine is not the treatment unless the cause is alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal.
lines: Glasses and hearing aids are ordered back to the bedside.
A sitter is safer than a restraint.
The family is told this is often reversible.
Diphenhydramine and other strong anticholinergics worsen cognition and are on the Beers list. Stop them rather than adding a cholinesterase inhibitor on top.
A new focal deficit is a stroke pathway. Do not attribute it to the dementia diagnosis.
miss: Ordering lorazepam every six hours for an older patient who is confused after a hip fracture.
diagramAlt: Beers drugs that cause admissions. Benzodiazepines for sleep or anxiety Strong anticholinergics, including diphenhydramine Sliding-scale insulin used alone

source.name: American Geriatrics Society 2023 Updated AGS Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults.
source.says: Drug-disease interaction: in dementia or cognitive impairment, avoid anticholinergics, benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, and chronic antipsychotics because of adverse CNS effects. Cumulative anticholinergic exposure is associated with falls, delirium, and dementia.

title: A brain abscess order is antibiotics and a surgeon, not a lumbar puncture
lead: Order antibiotics that cover the source and a surgical consult. Do not order a lumbar puncture as the diagnostic test.
lines: CT or MRI is the image.
The ear, the sinus, and the heart are examined.
A small abscess in a stable patient can be antibiotics and a short-interval scan, written as a plan.
Image before the lumbar puncture when a focal sign or papilledema is present.
Contiguous sinus or ear source is often streptococci.
miss: Ordering a lumbar puncture for a ring-enhancing lesion with a midline shift.

source.name: ESCMID guidelines on the diagnosis and treatment of brain abscess in children and adults.
source.says: MRI is recommended for diagnosis. Aspiration or excision of brain abscess is recommended whenever feasible, except for toxoplasmosis. Adjunctive glucocorticoids are recommended for severe symptoms from perifocal oedema or impending herniation.

title: Lithium admission: hold, hydrate, and a level timed correctly
lead: Hold lithium, start saline if the patient is dry, and time the level so you do not sample during the distribution phase and undercall the toxicity.
lines: Dialysis is ordered for severe neurotoxicity, not for a mild tremor.
The home dose is not restarted at discharge without a new level and a reason.
NSAIDs, thiazides, and ACE inhibitors raise the level. Hold lithium and recheck.
Severe neurotoxicity or a level well above the range is dialysis. Chronic use causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
miss: Restarting the home dose the next morning because the patient looks better.
diagramAlt: Lithium interactions. NSAIDs, thiazides, ACE inhibitors raise it Hold the drug. Severe toxicity: dialysis Chronic use: nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

source.name: EXTRIP. Extracorporeal Treatment for Lithium Poisoning: Systematic Review and Recommendations.
source.says: Extracorporeal treatment is recommended in severe lithium poisoning: if kidney function is impaired and the [Li+] is >4.0 mEq/L, or with a decreased level of consciousness, seizures, or life-threatening dysrhythmias irrespective of the [Li+]. It is suggested if the [Li+] is >5.0 mEq/L or significant confusion is present.

title: Serotonin syndrome: stop the new drug tonight
lead: The order is to discontinue every serotonergic drug on tonight's list, including the linezolid or the tramadol that was just added.
lines: A benzodiazepine is ordered for agitation.
Cyproheptadine is ordered if supportive care is failing.
Cooling is ordered if the temperature is high. Restraints alone are not.
Clonus and hyperreflexia within hours of an SSRI plus an MAOI, linezolid, tramadol, or a triptan. Stop both drugs on that shift.
A benzodiazepine treats the agitation. Cyproheptadine is the antagonist if support is not enough. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is rigidity over days, not clonus.
miss: Continuing the SSRI and adding another dose of tramadol for the shivering.
diagramAlt: NMS versus serotonin syndrome. NMS: lead-pipe, high CK, days Serotonin: clonus, hours, two drugs Stop the offending drug in both

source.name: StatPearls. Serotonin Syndrome.
source.says: The first step in managing serotonin syndrome is accurately and promptly recognizing the condition. Treatment involves discontinuing the offending medications and providing supportive care. If supportive measures, vital signs management, and chemical sedation do not adequately treat serotonin syndrome, then antidotes can be considered; cyproheptadine has 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A antagonistic properties.

title: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: stop the drug and check the CK
lead: Discontinue the antipsychotic and order a creatine kinase, a temperature, and cooling. Do not order another dose for agitation.
lines: Onset is days after a dopamine blocker. Lead-pipe rigidity, fever, and autonomic instability. CK is often in the thousands.
Reflexes are reduced. Clonus means serotonin syndrome, which starts in hours, not this picture.
Bromocriptine or dantrolene is adjunctive. Neither replaces stopping the drug. A benzodiazepine can cover agitation while it is held.
miss: Ordering haloperidol for the rigidity.
diagramAlt: NMS versus serotonin syndrome. NMS: lead-pipe, high CK, days Serotonin: clonus, hours, two drugs Stop the offending drug in both

source.name: StatPearls. Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
source.says: Treatment involves immediately discontinuing the offending agent, aggressive supportive care to manage and prevent complications, and pharmacologic therapy in severe cases. Supportive therapy includes aggressive cooling and correction of volume deficits and any electrolyte imbalances.

title: Bell palsy discharge is a steroid and an eye-care plan
lead: Discharge Bell palsy with a corticosteroid started today and instructions to lubricate the eye that does not close, including at night.
lines: Oral corticosteroids are strongly recommended within 72 hours of onset of peripheral facial nerve palsy.
Antivirals may be added. They are not a substitute for the corticosteroid.
Routine testing is unnecessary for a typical presentation. Atypical features are the reason to test further.
miss: Starting an antiviral without a corticosteroid, or starting the corticosteroid after 72 hours as if the window were still open.
diagramAlt: Bell palsy, first 72 hours. Forehead involved = peripheral nerve Prednisone early. Lubricate the eye Forehead spared = stroke pathway

source.name: Clinical practice guideline for the evaluation and management of peripheral facial nerve palsy (Korean multidisciplinary guideline).
source.says: Oral corticosteroids are strongly recommended within 72 hours of symptom onset (Grade A). Antivirals may be added based on clinical judgment and patient preference (Grade B). Routine testing is unnecessary for typical Bell's palsy; selective testing is advised for atypical features.

title: A cerebellar bleed is a surgical call, not a floor admission
lead: Admit a cerebellar hemorrhage to a setting that can operate, and call neurosurgery when you order the CT, not the next morning.
lines: Blood pressure orders follow hemorrhagic-stroke practice and avoid overcorrection.
Reverse anticoagulation if it is present.
A falling level of consciousness is an immediate call, not a note.
Cerebellar blood that compresses the brainstem or blocks the fourth ventricle is evacuated. It is not a floor observation.
Hypertensive sites are putamen, thalamus, pons, and cerebellum. A lobar bleed in an older adult is amyloid until proved otherwise.
miss: Admitting a cerebellar hemorrhage to a medical floor with neuro checks every 8 hours.
diagramAlt: Which bleed goes to surgery. Cerebellum with compression: evacuate Putamen: usually medical Lobar in an older adult: think amyloid

source.name: 2022 AHA/ASA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
source.says: For patients with cerebellar hemorrhage, indications for immediate surgical evacuation with or without an external ventricular drain to reduce mortality include larger volume (>15 mL) in addition to neurological deterioration, brainstem compression, and hydrocephalus.

title: Epidural hematoma: reverse, type and screen, operating room
lead: The orders for a deteriorating epidural hematoma are reversal of anticoagulation, a type and screen, and the operating room.
lines: An epidural hematoma larger than 30 mL is evacuated, whatever the Glasgow Coma Scale score.
A patient who was talking and is now worsening does not wait for the next scheduled scan.
The blood is lens-shaped and does not cross sutures. That shape is the middle meningeal artery.
miss: Watching an epidural hematoma over 30 mL because the patient is still speaking.

source.name: Brain Trauma Foundation. Surgical management of acute epidural hematomas.
source.says: An epidural hematoma (EDH) greater than 30 cm3 should be surgically evacuated regardless of the patient's Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score.

title: Subdural hematoma discharge is a reversed anticoagulant and a plan
lead: Any anticoagulant-associated subdural hematoma gets the anticoagulant reversed. A small collection does not stay on the drug.
lines: The Neurocritical Care Society and Society of Critical Care Medicine recommend reversal of antithrombotics in intracranial hemorrhage, including subdural hematoma.
A shift or a worsening exam is surgery. Reversal still happens for the collection that is only being watched.
The reason for the anticoagulant, such as a mechanical valve, changes when it may restart. It does not cancel the reversal.
Fall precautions and a named recheck of the scan are part of an observation plan.
miss: Leaving a small anticoagulant-associated subdural hematoma on the anticoagulant because the patient is in atrial fibrillation.

source.name: Guideline for Reversal of Antithrombotics in Intracranial Hemorrhage. Neurocritical Care Society and Society of Critical Care Medicine.
source.says: Rapid reversal of coagulopathy may help limit hematoma expansion and improve outcomes. The committee developed recommendations for reversal of vitamin K antagonists, direct factor Xa antagonists, direct thrombin inhibitors, unfractionated heparin, low-molecular weight heparin, heparinoids, and pentasaccharides.

title: Compartment syndrome: remove the cast and call surgery in one order
lead: The order is to bivalve or remove the cast and to call the surgeon for fasciotomy. Analgesia is given and does not replace the call.
lines: Document pain with passive stretch.
A present pulse is written down so nobody waits for it to vanish.
The limb is kept at the level of the heart, not dangling and not forgotten.
Pulselessness is late. Remove the cast and call for fasciotomy. More opioid is not the treatment.
miss: Increasing the morphine and leaving the tight cast on until morning rounds.
diagramAlt: Compartment, do not wait for the pulse. Pain out of proportion Pain on passive stretch Fasciotomy. Pulse loss is late

source.name: AAOS Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Acute Compartment Syndrome (case-based summary).
source.says: Serial clinical examinations can assist in ruling in acute compartment syndrome; compartment pressure monitoring can assist but is not always necessary. A diastolic-to-compartment pressure difference of 30 mm Hg can be used as a threshold for diagnosis and fasciotomy.

title: Hip fracture orders: pain, prophylaxis, and a surgical date
lead: Write pain control, venous-thromboembolism prophylaxis, and a surgical plan within about 48 hours for a medically ready hip fracture.
lines: Delirium precautions are on the order set: no diphenhydramine, glasses on, catheter out.
Consent and the medical issues that truly delay surgery are listed, not a vague clearance.
Prophylax against venous thromboembolism. A fragility fracture starts osteoporosis treatment before discharge. Remove the urinary catheter.
miss: Waiting five days for every consultant to say the word cleared.
diagramAlt: Hip fracture timing. Operate within about 48 hours if ready Prophylax against clot A fragility fracture starts osteoporosis treatment

source.name: NICE CG124. Hip fracture: management.
source.says: Perform surgery on the day of, or the day after, admission. Care should also follow NICE guidance on venous thromboembolism, delirium, and osteoporosis fragility-fracture risk assessment.

more.name: AAOS Management of Hip Fractures in Older Adults Clinical Practice Guideline (2021).

title: An open fracture is bone open to the outside
lead: An open fracture communicates with the skin. The bone is contaminated. That is a different wound from a closed fracture.
lines: The soft-tissue opening is what makes the fracture open, not the size of the bone piece on the film.
Dirt and skin flora are in the wound from the moment it happens.
A closed fracture does not have that communication.
miss: Splinting and arranging antibiotics with the morning surgical add-on list.

source.name: StatPearls. Open Fracture Management.
source.says: An open fracture is an injury where the fractured bone and/or fracture hematoma are exposed to the external environment via a traumatic violation of the soft tissue and skin.

title: Septic knee: tap, then wash, then narrow the drug
lead: Order the aspiration before the antibiotic if the patient is stable, then surgical washout, then narrow the antibiotic to the culture.
lines: A prosthetic joint is a different order: do not start a short oral course.
Gonorrhea swabs are added when the history fits.
Weight-bearing status is written so the joint is protected.
Then wash the joint. Gonorrhea is the exception in a young sexually active patient. A prosthetic joint is a biofilm operation, not a short oral course.
miss: Discharging a hot prosthetic knee on oral cephalexin.

source.name: StatPearls. Septic Arthritis.
source.says: Staphylococcus aureus is the most common organism in adults. Arthrocentesis should be done without delay; treatment is antimicrobial therapy with antistaphylococcal coverage plus joint drainage by aspiration, arthroscopy, or arthrotomy.

more.name: PIDS/IDSA guideline for acute bacterial arthritis in children (2024).

title: Gout flare orders name one anti-inflammatory and the kidney
lead: Order one anti-inflammatory the kidneys allow: an NSAID, colchicine, or a steroid. Do not order allopurinol as the only drug.
lines: The flare is treated with an anti-inflammatory. Allopurinol monotherapy is not flare treatment.
Colchicine is most useful in the first 36 hours. Reduce the dose when creatinine is high, and avoid it with a strong CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein inhibitor.
Continue allopurinol if it is already prescribed. Check the creatinine before an NSAID.
An opioid does not treat the crystal. A hot joint still needs the tap if septic arthritis is possible.
miss: Starting allopurinol alone and an opioid for a hot toe.
diagramAlt: Gout flare drug. Colchicine, NSAID, or glucocorticoid Not allopurinol as the only drug Continue allopurinol if already taking it

source.name: 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout.
source.says: For a gout flare, oral colchicine, NSAIDs, or glucocorticoids (oral, intraarticular, or intramuscular) are strongly recommended as first-line therapy, chosen by patient factors. Patients already taking urate-lowering therapy should continue it.

title: Back pain without a flag goes home without an MRI
lead: Discharge acute low back pain without a red flag with activity and no MRI. Write the flags that should bring the patient back.
lines: Cauda equina symptoms cancel the discharge and start an MRI today.
Opioids are not the default prescription.
Work advice is to move, not to stay in bed.
No MRI in the first 6 weeks without a red flag. Red flags: cancer, unexplained weight loss, fever, injection drug use, trauma, progressive deficit, saddle anesthesia, or new bowel or bladder loss.
Cauda equina is an MRI and decompression today. Activity, not bed rest, for ordinary pain.
miss: Ordering an MRI for two days of pain and prescribing bed rest.
diagramAlt: Image the back now. Cauda equina, cancer, infection, deficit Otherwise no MRI in the first weeks Activity, not bed rest

source.name: ACR Appropriateness Criteria. Low Back Pain: 2021 Update.
source.says: Uncomplicated acute low back pain with or without radiculopathy does not warrant imaging. Imaging is considered after up to 6 weeks of medical management with little or no improvement, or with red flags such as cauda equina syndrome, malignancy, fracture, or infection.

more.name: ACP Clinical Practice Guideline. Noninvasive Treatments for Acute, Subacute, and Chronic Low Back Pain (2017).

title: Giant-cell arteritis: steroid tonight, biopsy this week
lead: Start a high-dose glucocorticoid for every suspected giant cell arteritis, prednisone about 1 mg/kg up to 80 mg, and give an intravenous pulse if vision is threatened.
lines: If vision is threatened, give an intravenous glucocorticoid pulse rather than tablets alone.
Biopsy as soon as possible, ideally within 2 weeks of starting steroids. A later biopsy can still show arteritis.
Prefer a specimen longer than 1 cm. Do not wait for the sedimentation rate to give the first dose.
miss: Waiting for the biopsy, or for the sedimentation rate, before the first glucocorticoid dose.

source.name: 2021 American College of Rheumatology/Vasculitis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Giant Cell Arteritis and Takayasu Arteritis.
source.says: High dose oral glucocorticoids: prednisone 1 mg/kg up to 80 mg daily. With threatened vision loss, pulse intravenous glucocorticoids are conditionally recommended. A long-segment biopsy (>1 cm) is preferred, obtained within two weeks of starting oral glucocorticoids; a biopsy obtained later could still be informative.

title: Necrotizing fasciitis orders are the operating room and broad antibiotics
lead: Write an operating-room booking and broad antibiotics at the same time. Do not write a 24-hour trial.
lines: The recommendation is prompt diagnosis and timely effective treatment, not a day of antibiotics to see if the skin improves.
Pain beyond the visible skin, toxicity, and a rising lactate are the clinical clues. Crepitus is not required.
Pain beyond the skin you can see, with toxicity, goes to the operating room the same day. Antibiotics alone are not the plan.
miss: Observing suspected necrotizing fasciitis overnight on antibiotics alone.

source.name: IDSA Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: 2014 Update.
source.says: Prompt surgical consultation is recommended for aggressive infections with systemic toxicity or suspected necrotizing fasciitis or gas gangrene (strong). Empiric antibiotics should be broad, e.g., vancomycin or linezolid plus piperacillin-tazobactam or a carbapenem.

title: Ankylosing spondylitis discharge is an NSAID and an eye warning
lead: Discharge with an NSAID, a plan to stay active, and instructions to seek care the same day for a red painful eye.
lines: A TNF inhibitor is a follow-up decision, not the emergency-department start.
Do not prescribe prolonged bed rest.
Chest pain in this disease can be aortitis and is not ignored.
An NSAID is first-line. A red painful eye is acute anterior uveitis and is same-day ophthalmology.
miss: Prescribing two weeks of bed rest and no warning about the eye.

source.name: 2019 ACR/SAA/SPARTAN Recommendations for the Treatment of Ankylosing Spondylitis and Nonradiographic Axial Spondyloarthritis.
source.says: NSAIDs are strongly recommended over no NSAIDs, and physical therapy over no physical therapy. In active AS despite NSAIDs, a TNF inhibitor is strongly recommended over no TNF inhibitor.

title: Marfan discharge includes an aortic-imaging appointment
lead: Marfan syndrome is a clinical picture of aortic root dilatation, lens dislocation, and a long skeleton. The gene is FBN1.
lines: Severity runs from isolated features to severe disease in a newborn.
Mitral valve prolapse can be present and is not the aortic-root problem.
Eye findings include lens dislocation, cataract, and retinal detachment.
miss: Discharging a new diagnosis with reassurance about height and no plan to image the aorta.
diagramAlt: Marfan syndrome. FBN1 makes fibrillin Aortic root dilatation is the danger Lens dislocation is the eye finding

source.name: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease.
source.says: In patients with Marfan syndrome, a TTE is recommended at the time of initial diagnosis, to determine the diameters of the aortic root and ascending aorta, and 6 months thereafter, to determine the rate of aortic growth.

more.name: StatPearls. Marfan Syndrome (FBN1, eye and skeletal features).

title: Pemphigus admission includes a CD20-inhibitor plan
lead: Moderate-to-severe pemphigus is admitted for wound care and fluids, and a CD20 inhibitor is a first-line option in the international consensus.
lines: Infection of denuded skin is watched.
A steroid-sparing drug is a follow-up, not a reason to delay the steroid.
Bullous pemphigoid is not given the same intensity by reflex.
Systemic corticosteroid plus a steroid-sparing drug. Topical therapy alone does not treat widespread disease.
miss: Discharging widespread skin loss with a topical cream.

source.name: International consensus on pemphigus management (Joly et al.).
source.says: This international consensus includes intravenous CD20 inhibitors (rituximab, ofatumumab) as a first-line therapy option for moderate-to-severe pemphigus, alongside systemic corticosteroids.

title: Dermatomyositis discharge includes a cancer-screening plan
lead: An adult with new dermatomyositis leaves with immunosuppression started or arranged and a written cancer-screening plan.
lines: Breathlessness gets imaging before discharge if it is new.
The steroid is not the whole plan if the weakness is severe.
A statin is stopped if it is a possible contributor, and the rash is still explained.
Adults get a cancer search. Immunosuppression treats the muscle. A statin myopathy has no rash.
Gottron papules and a heliotrope rash plus proximal weakness.
miss: Prescribing prednisone with no follow-up and no cancer plan.

source.name: International Guideline for Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathy-Associated Cancer Screening (IMACS).
source.says: Dermatomyositis carries the highest cancer risk among myositis subtypes. All adults with new-onset myositis should be tested for myositis-specific and myositis-associated autoantibodies to stratify cancer risk, which then sets screening modality and frequency.

title: Chest-pain orders: ECG, aspirin, and oxygen only if hypoxic
lead: The first chest-pain orders are an ECG within 10 minutes, aspirin if it is safe, and oxygen only if the saturation is low.
lines: A STEMI activates the lab before the troponin.
Two large IVs are ordered if reperfusion or instability is likely.
A normal first ECG with ongoing pain gets a repeat, not a discharge.
Do not apply a nonrebreather when saturation is normal. Aspirin 162–325 mg, if there is no allergy or active bleeding, is the drug that is indicated.
miss: Waiting for a bed assignment to obtain the ECG.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: A 12-lead ECG should be acquired and interpreted within 10 minutes of first medical contact. Aspirin should be initiated with a loading dose (162-325 mg) as soon as possible on presentation. With oxygen saturation 90% or higher, routine supplemental oxygen is not recommended.

title: A STEMI transfer is a clock you write down
lead: When a STEMI presents at a hospital that cannot do PCI, write the transfer time goal of 120 minutes or give a fibrinolytic if that goal will be missed.
lines: Activate the receiving lab before the ambulance leaves.
Do not wait for the troponin to decide.
Document first medical contact, not just door time.
ECG within 10 minutes of first medical contact. Do not wait for troponin to activate the lab for ST elevation.
Device by 90 minutes at a PCI hospital. If transfer will miss 120 minutes, give a fibrinolytic. Oxygen only if saturation is low.
miss: Holding the patient for a morning catheterization slot at a hospital two hours away.
diagramAlt: ACS time goals. ECG within 10 minutes of contact PCI hospital: device by 90 minutes Transfer: 120 minutes, or give a lytic

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: For STEMI within 12 hours, primary PCI with an FMC-to-device target of 90 minutes or less at a PCI-capable hospital, or 120 minutes or less when transfer is required. Give fibrinolytic therapy if expected delay to primary PCI is more than 2 hours from FMC and there are no contraindications.

title: Heart-failure discharge starts the missing pillar
lead: Before a HFrEF discharge, start any of the four pillars that are missing and safe, and book follow-up within 7 days.
lines: The 2024 hospitalized-heart-failure pathway emphasizes starting them in the hospital.
A small creatinine rise is not a stop order on the discharge summary.
Daily weights and the salt plan are written in words the patient can use.
The four drugs are an ARNI (or ACE inhibitor or ARB if an ARNI cannot be used), carvedilol or metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol, an MRA, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.
miss: Discharging on a loop diuretic alone with a clinic visit in six weeks.
diagramAlt: Start before discharge. ARNI, evidence-based beta blocker MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor Clinic within 7 days

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: GDMT for HFrEF now includes 4 medication classes: renin-angiotensin system inhibition with ARNi, ACEi, or ARB; beta blockers; MRAs; and SGLT2i. Beta blockers with proven benefit are bisoprolol, carvedilol, and sustained-release metoprolol succinate.

more.name: 2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway for Patients Hospitalized With Heart Failure.

title: Improved ejection fraction is continued on the discharge list
lead: The discharge list for improved ejection fraction keeps the HFrEF drugs. Write do not stop on the summary.
lines: Name the beta blocker as succinate, carvedilol, or bisoprolol, not atenolol.
The reason each drug is on the list is one line, so the next clinician does not clean it up.
A low blood pressure that the patient tolerates is not an automatic stop.
The four drugs are an ARNI (or ACE inhibitor or ARB if an ARNI cannot be used), carvedilol or metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol, an MRA, and an SGLT2 inhibitor.
miss: Stopping the ARNI at discharge because the ejection fraction is now 50%.
diagramAlt: Start before discharge. ARNI, evidence-based beta blocker MRA and SGLT2 inhibitor Clinic within 7 days

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: Patients with HFrEF whose LVEF improves to above 40% have HFimpEF and should continue HFrEF treatment; GDMT should be continued to prevent relapse of HF and LV dysfunction, even if asymptomatic.

title: Atrial fibrillation discharge is a rate and a stroke drug
lead: Discharge atrial fibrillation with a rate plan and an anticoagulant if the yearly risk is about 2% or higher. Rhythm control is not required for the prescription.
lines: Write the DOAC dose for the kidney function you measured.
Aspirin is not the stroke prescription.
A mechanical valve or severe mitral stenosis is warfarin, and the summary says so.
Class 1 anticoagulation is an estimated risk of at least 2% per year: CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 or more in men and 3 or more in women.
miss: Sending the patient out on aspirin because the rhythm converted in the emergency department.
diagramAlt: Who gets anticoagulation. Class 1: ≥2% per year Men CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2, women ≥3 DOAC, except mitral stenosis or metal valve

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: For AF with an estimated annual thromboembolic risk of 2% or more per year (eg, CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or more in men, 3 or more in women), anticoagulation is recommended. DOACs are recommended over warfarin except with moderate to severe rheumatic mitral stenosis or a mechanical heart valve; aspirin is not an alternative.

title: New hypertension orders use two drugs when the pressure is 140/90 or higher
lead: For a confirmed pressure of 140/90 or higher, order two agents, preferably one pill, and a home-pressure follow-up.
lines: Use PREVENT if you are deciding on stage 1 treatment.
Do not use the 2017 pooled cohort equation in the note as if it were current.
A pregnancy test comes before an ACE inhibitor in a person who could be pregnant.
At least 140/90 mm Hg starts two agents from different classes, preferably one pill. Goal for most adults is under 130/80.
Stage 1 (130–139/80–89) starts a drug now if there is CVD, diabetes, CKD, or a PREVENT 10-year risk of at least 7.5%. Otherwise try 3–6 months of lifestyle.
miss: Starting hydrochlorothiazide alone at 168/102 and saying come back in three months.
diagramAlt: 2025 blood-pressure start. ≥140/90: two drugs, one pill if possible Goal under 130/80 for most adults Stage 1: drug now if PREVENT ≥7.5%

source.name: 2025 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults.
source.says: Stage 2 hypertension (140/90 or higher) starts drug therapy with 2 first-line agents of different classes, preferably as a single-pill combination. The goal is under 130/80 for all adults. Stage 1 starts a drug with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT 10-year risk of 7.5% or more; otherwise after a 3- to 6-month lifestyle trial.

title: Dissection orders: beta blocker, surgeon, no lytic
lead: Order a beta blocker, a surgical consult, and pain control for a suspected ascending dissection. Write no thrombolysis on the chart.
lines: A pure vasodilator is not the first blood-pressure drug.
Type and screen and large-bore access are ordered.
The CT is expedited. It is not a routine add-on.
Unequal arm pressures or pulses and tearing pain to the back. Give a beta blocker before a pure vasodilator.
Involvement of the ascending aorta is an operation. A fibrinolytic extends the tear.
miss: Activating the stroke or STEMI lytic pathway because the pain is severe.
diagramAlt: Ascending dissection. Beta blocker before a pure vasodilator Type A: operating room No fibrinolytic

source.name: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease.
source.says: Suspected or confirmed acute type A aortic dissection warrants emergency surgical consultation and immediate surgical intervention. Initial management of acute aortic syndrome includes intravenous beta blockers, adding intravenous vasodilators if BP is not controlled after beta-blocker therapy.

title: A rupturing aneurysm is blood bank and a surgeon
lead: Order a type and screen, large-bore access, and immediate surgical or endovascular consultation for a suspected rupture. Do not order a clinic ultrasound.
lines: Permissive hypotension until the aorta is controlled. A large crystalloid bolus before control can worsen bleeding.
Back or abdominal pain plus hypotension is rupture. That patient does not go to a clinic ultrasound.
A known diameter in the chart is retrieved. A tender pulsatile mass is not re-examined over and over.
miss: Ordering a clinic ultrasound, or bolusing to a normal blood pressure, before the aorta is controlled.

source.name: 2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease.
source.says: In ruptured AAA, permissive hypotension can be beneficial to decrease the rate of bleeding; rupture protocols aim at immediate transfer to the operating room for prompt hemorrhage control and repair.

more.name: Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines on the care of patients with an abdominal aortic aneurysm (2018).

title: Tamponade orders are fluids and drainage
lead: Order a fluid bolus as a bridge and pericardial drainage. Do not order furosemide.
lines: The echo is stat if the patient is not already crashing.
Reversal of anticoagulation is ordered if the effusion is bloody and the drug is on board.
A pericardial window is the plan if the fluid will reaccumulate.
Diastolic pressures equalize and the y descent drops. Pulsus paradoxus is an exaggerated inspiratory fall in systolic pressure.
Fluids are a bridge. Drainage is the treatment. A diuretic removes the last preload.
miss: Ordering a diuretic for the elevated neck veins.

source.name: 2015 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of pericardial diseases.
source.says: Treatment of cardiac tamponade is drainage of the pericardial fluid, preferably by needle pericardiocentesis with echocardiographic or fluoroscopic guidance, performed without delay in unstable patients (class I).

more.name: StatPearls. Cardiac Tamponade.

title: Torsades orders: magnesium, potassium, and stop the QT drug
lead: Order intravenous magnesium, a potassium, and discontinuation of the QT-prolonging drug. Defibrillate if the patient is unstable.
lines: Do not order amiodarone for pause-dependent polymorphic tachycardia with a long QT.
The offending antibiotic or antiemetic is named on the allergy or avoid list.
A congenital long QT gets a specialist before discharge if the patient presented with syncope.
Stop the QT-prolonging drug. Do not give amiodarone or another QT-prolonging antiarrhythmic for torsades.
miss: Ordering amiodarone and continuing the azithromycin.

source.name: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC. Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support.
source.says: Immediate unsynchronized shock is recommended for adults with sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (COR 1). Magnesium may be considered for treatment of adults with recurrences of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with a long QT interval (torsades de pointes) (COR 2b).

more.name: 2022 ESC Guidelines for ventricular arrhythmias and the prevention of sudden cardiac death.

title: Endocarditis orders: three cultures, then the drug if unstable
lead: Order three sets of blood cultures from separate sites. If the patient is unstable, the antibiotic follows the cultures immediately. If stable, wait for the draws.
lines: An echo is ordered. A transthoracic study may miss a small vegetation.
Dentist clearance is not today's order.
Hold anticoagulation decisions for a stroke until imaging says whether the infarct is hemorrhagic.
Acute on a normal valve is Staphylococcus aureus. Subacute on an abnormal valve is viridans streptococci.
Three culture sets from separate sites before antibiotics if the patient is stable. Prophylaxis is only for the highest-risk hearts, not for an isolated click.
miss: Giving an oral antibiotic in the clinic and culturing the blood the next day.
diagramAlt: Endocarditis cultures. Three sets, separate sticks Before antibiotics if the patient can wait Prophylaxis only for the highest-risk hearts

source.name: StatPearls. Infective Endocarditis.
source.says: Diagnosis uses blood cultures and echocardiography. AHA and ACC guidance limits antibiotic prophylaxis to patients at highest risk of adverse outcomes from endocarditis who undergo dental procedures that manipulate gingival or periapical tissue or perforate the oral mucosa.

more.name: 2015 AHA Scientific Statement. Infective Endocarditis in Adults.

title: A tet spell order is knees, oxygen, and a vasoconstrictor if it continues
lead: Order calming, knee-chest position, oxygen, and a vasoconstrictor if the spell continues. Do not order a vasodilator.
lines: The murmur softening is recorded.
Morphine or a similar calming drug is part of some pathways. The point is the resistance.
The surgical team that knows this heart is called.
Pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular hypertrophy, overriding aorta, VSD. A spell is infundibular spasm.
Knees-to-chest raises systemic resistance and sends blood to the lungs. A vasodilator does the opposite. The murmur gets softer as less blood crosses the valve.
miss: Giving a drug that drops afterload during a spell.
diagramAlt: Hypercyanotic spell. Knees to chest. Oxygen. Calm Raise systemic resistance A vasodilator worsens the right-to-left shunt

source.name: StatPearls. Tetralogy of Fallot.
source.says: Tet spells need knee-chest positioning to increase systemic vascular resistance, oxygen, and sometimes intravenous beta-blockers or intravenous phenylephrine to increase systemic afterload. Morphine can be given as a sedative.

title: Coarctation follow-up is a leg pressure at every visit
lead: After coarctation repair, every visit includes a leg blood pressure and a question about headaches and exercise. Residual or recurrent narrowing is how these patients present as adults.
lines: A bicuspid valve is listened for.
Hypertension can persist after a good repair and is still treated to the adult goal.
Pregnancy is planned with a cardiologist.
Higher pressure in the arms than the legs and a radio-femoral delay. Rib notching is collateral flow and is late.
Turner syndrome is the association in girls. A bicuspid aortic valve often sits with the coarct.
miss: Treating an arm pressure of 150 and never checking the leg.

source.name: StatPearls. Coarctation of the Aorta.
source.says: In older children and adults, aortic coarctation typically manifests as upper extremity hypertension. Despite successful short-term outcomes, continuous monitoring is necessary to manage residual risks such as recoarctation and aneurysm formation.

more.name: 2018 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Adults With Congenital Heart Disease.

title: HFpEF admission is decongestion and the SGLT2 inhibitor
lead: Admit HFpEF for decongestion and continue or start an SGLT2 inhibitor. Do not build a HFrEF four-drug list the patient does not have an indication for.
lines: Diurese the congestion. An SGLT2 inhibitor has a class 2a recommendation in HFpEF.
Do not copy carvedilol, a mineralocorticoid antagonist, and an ARNI onto every preserved-EF admission.
Control the blood pressure to the current adult goal, and control atrial fibrillation because it steals filling time.
Daily weights go on the discharge list. A rising creatinine from over-diuresis is a reason to pause the loop, not to add the HFrEF stack.
miss: Adding carvedilol, spironolactone, and an ARNI to every preserved-ejection-fraction admission.
diagramAlt: HFpEF versus HFrEF. HFpEF: EF ≥50%, filling problem SGLT2 inhibitor has a recommendation Do not copy all four HFrEF drugs blindly

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: New recommendations for HF with preserved EF are made for SGLT2i (COR 2a), MRAs (COR 2b), and ARNi (COR 2b). In HFpEF, SGLT2i can be beneficial in decreasing HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality.

title: Flutter discharge includes stroke prevention
lead: Discharge typical flutter with a rate or rhythm plan and the same stroke-prevention decision you would make for fibrillation.
lines: Isthmus ablation is the referral, written with a time.
Anticoagulation is not stopped because today's ECG is sinus.
The sawtooth is named in the summary so the next clinician does not call it sinus tachycardia.
Typical flutter is cavotricuspid-isthmus macro-reentry. A ventricular rate of 150 with sawtooth waves is 2:1 conduction.
Ablation of the isthmus treats the circuit. Stroke prevention follows the same risk threshold as fibrillation and is not cancelled by sinus rhythm.
miss: Stopping the DOAC after a flutter cardioversion.

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: Anticoagulation is recommended for an estimated annual thromboembolic risk of 2% or more (eg, CHA2DS2-VASc 2 or more in men, 3 or more in women), with DOACs over warfarin except moderate to severe rheumatic mitral stenosis or a mechanical valve. Patients after flutter ablation are not free from thromboembolic risk.

more.name: StatPearls. Atrial Flutter.

title: Rheumatic prophylaxis is a scheduled penicillin, written for years
lead: Write the secondary-prevention penicillin as a scheduled drug with a duration, not as a one-time course.
lines: The valve findings are in the summary.
A new sore throat is still treated and is not a reason to stop prophylaxis.
Dental care is encouraged. Prophylaxis for dental work is a separate, narrower indication.
Mitral valve is the most affected. Jones criteria diagnose acute rheumatic fever. The chronic valve lesion is years later.
miss: Writing take until gone on a 10-day amoxicillin course and no further plan.
diagramAlt: Rheumatic prophylaxis. After rheumatic fever: scheduled penicillin Duration depends on carditis One 10-day course is not prophylaxis

source.name: AHA Scientific Statement. Prevention of rheumatic fever and diagnosis and treatment of acute streptococcal pharyngitis.
source.says: A person who has had rheumatic fever is at very high risk of recurrence after GAS pharyngitis and needs continuous antimicrobial prophylaxis (secondary prevention). Duration depends on number of attacks, time since the last attack, exposure risk, age, and cardiac involvement.

title: A mechanical valve's warfarin is not swapped for a DOAC at discharge
lead: The discharge anticoagulant for a mechanical valve or for moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis is warfarin. Do not substitute a DOAC on the medication reconciliation.
lines: The INR target is the valve's target and is written as a number.
Aspirin may be added for some valves. It does not replace warfarin.
A DOAC on the home list of a mechanical valve is an error you correct.
miss: Reconciling apixaban onto a mechanical mitral valve because the patient prefers it.
diagramAlt: Who still needs warfarin. Mechanical valve Moderate or severe mitral stenosis A DOAC is otherwise preferred in AF

source.name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation.
source.says: In AF with rheumatic mitral stenosis or mitral stenosis of moderate or greater severity, long-term warfarin is recommended over DOACs. Warfarin remains first-line therapy with a mechanical heart valve. In other valve disease, DOACs are recommended over VKAs.

more.name: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Valvular Heart Disease.

title: Unstable angina is admitted for serial ECGs
lead: Rest pain without a troponin rise is admitted or observed for serial ECGs. It is not a clinic appointment tomorrow.
lines: Aspirin is given if it is safe.
A repeat ECG is timed, not left to chance.
A truly stable, brief, exertional pain with a normal ECG is a different, faster outpatient path.
Obtain a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes. Primary PCI targets are 90 minutes at a PCI-capable hospital and 120 minutes when transfer is required.
Give aspirin if it is safe. A repeat ECG is timed. Do not wait for the troponin to call a STEMI if the ST segments are already up.
miss: Discharging rest pain because the first troponin was negative.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: In suspected ACS, a 12-lead ECG should be acquired and interpreted within 10 minutes of first medical contact. Suspected STEMI goes to a PCI-capable hospital with an FMC-to-first-device goal of 90 minutes or less; direct transport may be considered if the anticipated FMC-to-device time is 120 minutes or less.

more.name: Medscape guideline summary of the 2025 ACC/AHA ACS guideline

title: Dilated cardiomyopathy discharge names the alcohol stop
lead: If alcohol caused the dilated cardiomyopathy, the discharge order says stop drinking, in plain words, and continues the heart-failure drugs if the ejection fraction is low.
lines: The ejection fraction is on the summary so the drugs are not cleaned off.
A viral or chemotherapy cause is named if that is the history.
Follow-up imaging is dated.
If alcohol is the cause, stopping it is the disease-modifying order. A low EF still gets the four-drug HFrEF regimen.
miss: A diuretic prescription and no mention of alcohol.

source.name: StatPearls. Dilated Cardiomyopathy.
source.says: Secondary causes include infectious myocarditis, ischemic disease, hypertension, anthracyclines, alcohol abuse, HIV, peripartum cardiomyopathy, or infiltrative disease. ACE inhibitors or ARBs are recommended in patients with DCM.

title: Restrictive disease: order light chains before another diuretic increase
lead: A thick ventricle with low electrocardiographic voltage gets a light-chain order before you keep increasing the diuretic. Amyloid is the diagnosis you are missing.
lines: Diuresis still treats congestion. It is not the only order.
Digoxin is used cautiously if amyloid is likely, because the drug binds the amyloid.
The heart-failure clinic is not a substitute for the protein studies.
Normal or near-normal EF with a stiff ventricle. Amyloid: thick walls and low QRS voltage.
miss: A third increase in the loop diuretic and no protein studies.

source.name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure.
source.says: In patients with a clinical suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis, screening for serum and urine monoclonal light chains with serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis and serum free light chains are recommended. If there is no evidence of monoclonal light chains, bone scintigraphy is used.

more.name: StatPearls. Restrictive Cardiomyopathy.

title: Do not order endocarditis prophylaxis for an ordinary mitral valve prolapse
