lead: An isolated mitral valve click does not get an endocarditis-prophylaxis order. Reserve prophylaxis for the short list of high-risk hearts.
lines: The click is documented so the next clinician does not call it a new murmur.
Severe regurgitation is followed. The click alone is not an operation.
A dental problem is treated by the dentist. A standing amoxicillin prescription is not the plan.
Acute on a normal valve is Staphylococcus aureus. Subacute on an abnormal valve is viridans streptococci.
Three culture sets from separate sites before antibiotics if the patient is stable. Prophylaxis is only for the highest-risk hearts, not for an isolated click.
miss: Writing take 2 g of amoxicillin before every cleaning for a mid-systolic click.
diagramAlt: Endocarditis cultures. Three sets, separate sticks Before antibiotics if the patient can wait Prophylaxis only for the highest-risk hearts

source.name: Prevention of Viridans Group Streptococcal Infective Endocarditis: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
source.says: There are no recommended changes to the 2007 VGS IE prevention guidelines. We continue to recommend VGS IE prophylaxis only for categories of patients at highest risk for adverse outcome while emphasizing the critical role of good oral health and regular access to dental care for all.

title: COPD exacerbation orders: steroid, oxygen target, and selective antibiotics
lead: Order a short systemic steroid, titrated oxygen, and antibiotics only if sputum purulence comes with more dyspnea or volume. Order noninvasive ventilation if the pH is acid and the CO2 is high.
lines: Continue or start the long-acting inhalers before discharge.
A chest film looks for pneumonia and pneumothorax.
Follow-up is days, not a month, after a hospitalization.
Group A: bronchodilator. Group B and group E: LABA plus LAMA. One moderate or severe exacerbation in the past year is group E.

Do not start LABA/ICS alone. Consider triple therapy when eosinophils are at least 300/µL. A flare gets a systemic steroid for about 5 days. Antibiotics if purulence plus more dyspnea or sputum volume.
miss: Ordering a 14-day antibiotic and high-flow oxygen for every wheeze.
diagramAlt: GOLD 2027, who gets ICS. 1 exacerbation = group E Start LABA + LAMA, not LABA/ICS Triple therapy if eosinophils ≥300

source.name: GOLD 2027 Report. Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD.
source.says: For exacerbations, 40 mg prednisone-equivalent daily for 5 days is recommended. Antibiotics are given with at least two of increased dyspnea, fever, sputum volume, and sputum purulence when purulence is one of them, or when ventilation is required.

title: Asthma admission: oxygen only under 92, steroid if severe
lead: Order oxygen only if saturation is under 92, with a target at or under 95. Order a systemic steroid for a severe attack and the patient's ICS-formoterol plan at discharge.
lines: A nonrebreather is not the default.
Review the inhaler technique before discharge.
Anaphylaxis, if present, gets epinephrine first.
No SABA-only plan. Track 1 uses as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol at steps 1–2, and the same inhaler as maintenance from step 3.
Oxygen is restricted to saturation below 92% with an upper target of 95%. Severe attacks receive a systemic corticosteroid, and the preventer is in place at discharge.
miss: Putting every asthma patient on 15 liters and discharging without a steroid inhaler.
diagramAlt: Acute asthma oxygen. No oxygen if saturation ≥92% If given, target ≤95% in adults Preferred reliever: ICS-formoterol

source.name: GINA 2026 Summary Guide for Asthma Management and Prevention.
source.says: In acute asthma, give oxygen when saturation on room air is under 92% and titrate it to a target saturation of 92-95%. The preferred reliever is ICS-formoterol; SABA-only treatment is not recommended.

title: Pneumonia orders name the bed and the bug coverage separately
lead: Write the site of care from hypoxia, pressure, and confusion, then the antibiotic that matches that site. Do not add metronidazole by default.
lines: Severe disease is a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or a fluoroquinolone.
A CURB-65 score is a note, not a substitute for looking at the patient.
Outpatient, no comorbidity: amoxicillin or doxycycline. A macrolide alone only where pneumococcal resistance is under 25%.
Do not add anaerobic coverage because the note says aspiration. Blood cultures are for severe disease.
miss: Admitting a comfortable patient with a normal saturation for intravenous antibiotics, or sending a hypoxic patient home.
diagramAlt: Pneumonia: where and which drug. Hypoxia, shock, or confusion: admit Severe: beta-lactam + macrolide No routine anaerobic drug for aspiration

source.name: 2019 ATS/IDSA Guideline for Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with Community-acquired Pneumonia.
source.says: Outpatients: amoxicillin or doxycycline; a macrolide only where pneumococcal resistance is under 25%. Use the PSI with clinical judgment for site of care. Anaerobic coverage is not routinely added for suspected aspiration unless lung abscess or empyema is suspected. Severe CAP: a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or a respiratory fluoroquinolone.

title: A stable embolus goes home or to the floor on a DOAC, not a lytic
lead: Order a DOAC for a stable pulmonary embolus if the bleeding risk allows it. Order a lytic only if the pressure is down or the patient is in shock.
lines: If the scan is delayed and suspicion is high, the anticoagulant is ordered now.
Right-heart strain is written in the note and does not by itself order the lytic.
Follow-up for provocation and cancer is named, not done as a full-body scan tonight.
Systolic pressure under 90 mm Hg or shock is high-risk and gets reperfusion. A normal pressure gets anticoagulation.
miss: Ordering systemic thrombolysis because the CT said saddle.
diagramAlt: Pulmonary embolism split. Hypotension or shock: reperfuse Normal pressure: anticoagulate Right-heart strain alone is not a lytic

source.name: 2026 AHA/ACC/Multisociety Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism in Adults (Guideline-at-a-Glance).
source.says: In PE categories A1-C2 (normotensive), systemic thrombolysis should not be used over anticoagulation alone because of bleeding and intracranial hemorrhage risk. DOACs are recommended over VKAs for patients eligible for oral anticoagulation.

more.name: 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism

title: SGLT2 inhibitor: hold tonight if the patient is not eating
lead: If the patient is fasting, going to surgery, or critically ill, hold the SGLT2 inhibitor tonight and write when to restart it. Do not discontinue it for a 4-point eGFR dip.
lines: Hold the SGLT2 inhibitor when the patient is not eating, before surgery, and in critical illness, because of ketoacidosis.
The early eGFR dip of a few mL/min is hemodynamic. It is not, by itself, a reason to stop the drug.
Check ketones if the patient is nauseated and the glucose is not very high. Euglycemic ketoacidosis is the miss.
Write the indication, heart failure or kidney disease, on the summary so the drug is restarted when the patient is eating.
miss: Continuing the SGLT2 inhibitor through a nothing-by-mouth day and an operation.
diagramAlt: SGLT2 inhibitor rules. Start at eGFR ≥20 if diabetes + CKD Also if HF, or ACR ≥200 mg/g Hold if fasting, surgery, or critical illness

source.name: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease.
source.says: It is reasonable to withhold SGLT2i during prolonged fasting, surgery, or critical medical illness, when people may be at greater risk for ketosis. Once started, continue even if eGFR falls below 20 unless not tolerated or KRT starts.

title: Hyponatremia seizure: a bolus of 3% and a recheck
lead: Order a bolus of hypertonic saline for a seizure from hyponatremia and recheck the sodium immediately. Do not order a slow correction as the only order.
lines: US expert panel: 100 mL of 3% saline over 10 minutes, up to three boluses.
European regimen: 150 mL of 3% saline over 20 minutes, repeated up to twice.
Aim for a 4 to 6 mmol/L rise in the first hour, then recheck.
Stop if the 24-hour rise will pass 10 mmol/L. That is the osmotic demyelination risk.
miss: Over-correcting by more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours, which risks osmotic demyelination.
diagramAlt: Severely symptomatic hyponatremia. US: 100 mL 3% over 10 min, up to x3 EU: 150 mL over 20 min, repeat x2 First hour: rise of 4-6 mmol/L Over 10 mmol/L in 24 h risks ODS

source.name: European clinical practice guideline on diagnosis and treatment of hyponatraemia (ESE/ESICM/ERA-EDTA).
source.says: Severe symptoms: prompt IV infusion of 150 mL 3% hypertonic saline over 20 minutes, repeated twice or until a 5 mmol/L rise. Limit the rise to 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours and 8 mmol/L every 24 hours thereafter.

more.name: Verbalis JG et al. Diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of hyponatremia: expert panel recommendations (US, 2013).

title: Diabetes insipidus orders: let them drink or replace the water
lead: Order free access to water or a matched intravenous replacement, and desmopressin only if the trial showed a central cause.
lines: A sodium is checked after each desmopressin dose.
Nephrogenic disease from lithium does not get escalating desmopressin.
The urine output is recorded hourly until it is stable.
Nephrogenic disease, including lithium, does not respond. Do not fluid-restrict a hypernatremic patient.
Desmopressin concentrates the urine only if the cause is central.
miss: Restricting a hypernatremic patient to 1 liter a day.

source.name: StatPearls. Arginine Vasopressin Disorder (Diabetes Insipidus).
source.says: After water deprivation, desmopressin increases urine osmolality by more than 100% in complete central DI and up to 50% in partial central DI. In adults, nephrogenic (AVP-resistance) disease is mostly from chronic lithium or hypercalcemia.

title: Tension pneumothorax compresses venous return
lead: A crashing patient with a shifted trachea has pressure in the pleural space being transmitted to the mediastinum. The film is not what explains the shock.
lines: Oxygen and large-bore access are ordered with it.
The side is written in the order so the wrong side is not opened.
A stable simple pneumothorax can have the film.
miss: Ordering a two-view chest radiograph stat on a patient with a pressure of 70 and a shifted trachea.

source.name: StatPearls. Tension Pneumothorax.
source.says: Tension pneumothorax is intrapleural air under pressure causing lung collapse and mediastinal shift; diagnosis is clinical, with hypotension, unilateral breath sounds, distended neck veins, and tracheal deviation.

title: ARDS ventilator orders use height, not the scale
lead: Order tidal volume from predicted body weight using height and sex, about 6 mL per kilogram, and a plateau-pressure limit of 30.
lines: Write the height in the order so the next respiratory therapist does not use actual weight.
A high CO2 is tolerated.
Fluids are conservative once shock is resuscitated.
Bilateral infiltrates not explained by left-atrial pressure. Tidal volume 6 mL/kg predicted body weight from height and sex.
Plateau pressure at or under 30 cm H2O. A PaCO2 of 50 can be accepted. Do not use actual body weight.
miss: Ordering 700 mL breaths because the patient weighs 120 kilograms.
diagramAlt: ARDS tidal volume. 6 mL/kg predicted body weight Use height and sex, not the scale Plateau pressure ≤30 cm H2O

source.name: ATS/ESICM/SCCM Clinical Practice Guideline: Mechanical Ventilation in Adult Patients with ARDS (Summary for Clinicians).
source.says: Adults with ARDS should receive mechanical ventilation that limits tidal volumes to 4-8 mL/kg predicted body weight and inspiratory plateau pressure to under 30 cm H2O (strong recommendation).

more.name: ARDS Network. Ventilation with lower tidal volumes (NEJM 2000).

title: Pulmonary fibrosis discharge is oxygen if hypoxic and an antifibrotic referral
lead: Discharge idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis with oxygen if the saturation requires it, pulmonary rehabilitation, and a referral for an antifibrotic. Do not discharge on a prednisone taper as the disease treatment.
lines: Vaccines are updated.
A new exposure or a connective-tissue symptom reopens the diagnosis.
Transplant referral is for the patient who is early enough to benefit.
Basal, peripheral honeycombing and Velcro crackles. Exclude connective-tissue disease and exposures before calling it idiopathic.
Nintedanib or pirfenidone is the disease-modifying choice. Long-term prednisone is not that treatment.
miss: A 40-milligram prednisone taper as the only discharge drug.
diagramAlt: IPF drug. Nintedanib or pirfenidone Not long-term prednisone as the disease drug Oxygen if hypoxemic

source.name: ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (an update) and Progressive Pulmonary Fibrosis in Adults.
source.says: Antifibrotic treatment is indicated for patients diagnosed with IPF; nintedanib and pirfenidone were recommended for IPF in prior guidelines and slow disease progression.

more.name: ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT IPF treatment guideline (2015)

title: Bronchiectasis discharge teaches clearance
lead: Discharge bronchiectasis with a written airway-clearance plan and an antibiotic only for this flare. Name the follow-up that looks for the cause.
lines: Sputum culture is sent before the antibiotic if the patient can produce it.
A vest or a breathing technique is specified, not the word clearance.
Smoking cessation is ordered if it applies.
Daily airway clearance is the treatment of the anatomy. Antibiotics treat a flare or a cultured Pseudomonas, not the dilated bronchi.
CT shows tram tracks and the signet-ring sign. A normal chest film does not exclude it.
miss: A rotating antibiotic calendar and no clearance instruction.

source.name: ERS clinical practice guideline for the management of adult bronchiectasis.
source.says: Strong recommendations favor airway clearance for most patients, long-term macrolides for those at high exacerbation risk, and long-term inhaled antibiotics with chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection at high exacerbation risk.

title: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis discharge names the antigen to remove
lead: The discharge instruction names the bird, the hot tub, or the barn to leave. A steroid prescription without that sentence is incomplete.
lines: Work exposure is a written restriction if that is the antigen.
Oxygen is ordered if the saturation requires it.
Follow-up imaging is timed.
Hours after birds, mold, or a barn. Removing the antigen is required. A steroid without removal fails.
Chronic disease scars the mid and upper lungs. Name the antigen in the discharge instructions.
miss: A steroid taper and a return to the same coop.

source.name: ATS/JRS/ALAT Clinical Practice Guideline. Diagnosis of Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis in Adults.
source.says: Patients with nonfibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis who avoid ongoing exposure to the inciting agent may have a favorable prognosis, with possible stabilization or full recovery.

title: Hyperkalemia with ECG changes: calcium first
lead: If the ECG shows peaked T waves or a wide QRS, order intravenous calcium first, then a shift, then a removal. A number without an ECG still gets a removal plan.
lines: ECG changes: calcium gluconate 1 g IV, and repeat it if the ECG stays abnormal.
Shift potassium with insulin plus dextrose, and with nebulized albuterol.
Recheck glucose after insulin. Hypoglycemia is the harm of that step.
Remove potassium with sodium zirconium cyclosilicate or patiromer, or with dialysis if the kidney cannot.
miss: Ordering calcium resonium, or only a binder, for a wide QRS.
diagramAlt: Hyperkalemia on US boards. Calcium gluconate 1 g IV, may repeat Insulin with dextrose, plus albuterol Then SZC or patiromer, or dialysis

source.name: Lindner G et al. Acute hyperkalemia in the emergency department: a summary from a Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes conference.
source.says: The ECG is a mainstay in managing hyperkalemia. Membrane stabilization by calcium salts and potassium-shifting agents, such as insulin and salbutamol, is the cornerstone in the acute management of hyperkalemia. However, only dialysis, potassium-binding agents, and loop diuretics remove potassium from the body.

title: Under 2.5 mmol/L of potassium is the severe band
lead: Severe hypokalemia, under 2.5 mmol/L, can cause an arrhythmia. Weakness and palpitations scale with how low the value is.
lines: A serum potassium of about 3.5 mmol/L is the lower limit of normal in this chapter.
3 to 3.4 mmol/L is mild, 2.5 to 3 is moderate, and under 2.5 mmol/L is severe.
Weakness, cramps, and palpitations follow the severity. Arrhythmia is the severe risk.
The serum value is a small fraction of body stores, so it does not measure total potassium.
miss: Calling a potassium of 2.4 mmol/L mild, or judging total body stores from the serum value alone.
diagramAlt: Hypokalemia severity. Floor about 3.5 mmol/L Mild 3 to 3.4; moderate 2.5 to 3 Severe: under 2.5 mmol/L

source.name: StatPearls. Hypokalemia.
source.says: An acceptable lower limit of normal serum potassium is 3.5 mmol/L. A level of 2.5 to 3 mmol/L is moderate, and below 2.5 mmol/L is severe hypokalemia.

title: Symptomatic hypocalcemia is calcium gluconate and a magnesium
lead: Order calcium gluconate for tetany, a seizure, or a long QT, and order a magnesium level with it.
lines: Recheck the calcium after the dose.
A post-thyroidectomy patient has the calcium ordered on a schedule, not after the first twitch.
Correct a low albumin before you treat a paper-low total calcium in a comfortable patient.
Prolonged QT, Chvostek or Trousseau sign, tetany, or a seizure gets intravenous calcium. Recheck magnesium.
A low albumin lowers total calcium without changing the ionized value.
miss: A one-time oral calcium for a seizing post-operative patient.
diagramAlt: Symptomatic hypocalcemia. Long QT, tetany, or seizure: IV calcium Check magnesium with it Post-thyroidectomy: scheduled calcium checks

source.name: Society for Endocrinology Emergency Endocrine Guidance: Emergency management of acute hypocalcaemia in adult patients.
source.says: Severe hypocalcaemia (under 1.9 mmol/L and/or symptomatic) is a medical emergency: give 10-20 mL 10% calcium gluconate IV over 10 minutes with ECG monitoring, repeated until asymptomatic, then a calcium gluconate infusion.

more.name: StatPearls. Hypocalcemia.

title: Respiratory acidosis: a ventilation order, not an oxygen order
lead: Order noninvasive ventilation or intubation for an acidemic, hypercapnic patient who is tiring. Do not order only a higher oxygen flow.
lines: A reversible sedative is stopped.
The chronic bicarbonate is respected so you do not overshoot.
A blood gas is timed after the ventilation starts.
Noninvasive ventilation is first if the airway is protected and the patient is not in shock.
miss: Turning the nasal cannula from 2 liters to 8 liters as the treatment of a pH of 7.15.
diagramAlt: When to start NIV. COPD flare with low pH and high CO2 Patient must protect the airway Oxygen alone does not clear CO2

source.name: GOLD 2027 Report. Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD.
source.says: NIV is the initial mode of ventilation for acute respiratory failure in COPD exacerbations; it improves acute respiratory acidosis, increasing pH and decreasing PaCO2, and reduces mortality and intubation rates.

more.name: StatPearls. Respiratory Acidosis.

title: Metabolic alkalosis: saline if the urine chloride is low
lead: Order saline and potassium when the urine chloride is low. Do not order saline for a high urine chloride from aldosterone.
lines: A chloride is on the chemistry, not assumed.
Acetazolamide is a selected order when volume cannot be given.
Saline will not fix hyperaldosteronism. Potassium is low in both and is replaced.
miss: A liter of saline for a hypertensive patient with a urine chloride of 40 and a renin that is suppressed.

source.name: StatPearls. Physiology, Metabolic Alkalosis.
source.says: Chloride-responsive metabolic alkalosis has urine chloride under 10 mEq/L and is treated by repleting chloride, potassium, and fluid; chloride-resistant alkalosis (urine chloride over 20 mEq/L) is treated by addressing the cause, such as aldosterone excess.

title: Hypernatremia orders replace water on a schedule
lead: Order free-water replacement with a rate and a sodium check, not a single open bag. The drop is gradual.
lines: Desmopressin is added only for proven central diabetes insipidus.
The patient who can drink is allowed to.
A sodium is on the morning labs and sooner if the replacement is intravenous.
Concentrated urine means the kidney is holding water and intake was the problem. Dilute urine is diabetes insipidus.
miss: An open order for D5W at 250 mL an hour with no recheck.
diagramAlt: Hypernatremia pace. Free-water deficit, replaced slowly Recheck sodium. Do not drop it overnight Desmopressin only if central DI

source.name: StatPearls. Hypernatremia.
source.says: Hypernatremia is corrected by calculating the free water deficit, replaced over 48 to 72 hours with a fall in serum sodium not exceeding 0.5 mEq per hour, with close monitoring of correction rate, urine output, and ongoing losses.

title: Adult polycystic disease: image a sudden headache
lead: Order urgent brain imaging for a sudden severe headache in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease. The blood pressure is treated at the same visit.
lines: Do not biopsy the kidney to confirm a diagnosis the family history and the ultrasound already made.
Tolvaptan, if used, comes with a liver-test plan.
A hematuria after minor trauma is rest and follow-up, not a cancer panic, unless it persists.
Autosomal dominant disease: bilateral cysts, hypertension, and intracranial aneurysms. Do not biopsy to diagnose it.
A thunderclap headache is imaged the same day. Autosomal recessive disease is the infantile form with congenital hepatic fibrosis.
miss: Scheduling a routine clinic MRI of the brain for next month after a thunderclap headache.

source.name: StatPearls. Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
source.says: Tolvaptan slows ADPKD progression by blocking vasopressin signaling at the V2 receptor. Blood pressure is treated, with a HALT-PKD target under 120-125/80 mm Hg, and lower targets in preserved GFR.

more.name: KDIGO 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline for ADPKD

title: Uric acid colic: alkalinize and do not trust the plain film
lead: Order urine alkalinization and pain control for a uric acid stone. Do not discharge on the basis of a clear abdominal film.
lines: A CT or ultrasound is the image if you need to see it.
Allopurinol is not the acute pain drug.
Strain the urine and the follow-up is written.
Plain films miss uric acid stones.
miss: Telling the patient the stone is gone because the KUB is negative.

source.name: StatPearls. Uric Acid Nephrolithiasis.
source.says: Uric acid stones are radiolucent. Almost two-thirds can be dissolved by increasing urinary pH and volume and lowering hyperuricosuria; potassium citrate is usually the preferred alkalinizing agent.

more.name: AUA guideline: Medical Management of Kidney Stones

title: Phosphate binders are timed with meals on the discharge list
lead: Write the phosphate binder with meals, in those words. A bedtime-only instruction does not bind phosphate.
lines: The dietitian order is part of the discharge.
Calcium and phosphate are both on the follow-up labs.
An SGLT2 inhibitor for the CKD indication is a separate line and is not the binder.
Phosphate rises, active vitamin D falls, PTH rises. Binders are taken with meals. A bedtime-only dose binds nothing.
Calcium-based binders add a calcium load. Watch the calcium-phosphate product.
miss: Take one tablet at bedtime on the prescription.
diagramAlt: Phosphate binder timing. Swallow with the meal Bedtime-only dosing binds nothing Watch the calcium-phosphate product

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD).
source.says: For persistently high serum phosphate despite dietary restriction, phosphate binders taken with meals are recommended; patients should understand the binder types and the importance of taking them with meals.

title: Renal-artery stenosis: recheck creatinine after the ACE inhibitor
lead: If you start an ACE inhibitor in suspected bilateral renal-artery stenosis or a solitary kidney, order a creatinine within days. A young woman with fibromuscular disease is referred for revascularization rather than stented by habit.
lines: The blood pressure still needs treatment.
A bruit is documented and is not the whole diagnosis.
Recheck creatinine within days of starting an ACE inhibitor. A sharp drop means both kidneys, or a single kidney, depend on the stenosis.
Fibromuscular dysplasia in a young woman is the lesion that is often opened. Atherosclerotic stenosis in an older smoker is not automatically stented.
miss: Starting lisinopril and scheduling the next creatinine in six months.

source.name: StatPearls. Renal Artery Stenosis.
source.says: Fibromuscular dysplasia responds more favorably to angioplasty than atherosclerotic renal artery stenosis, and these patients do not require stenting.

title: Emphysematous pyelonephritis is admitted for drainage
lead: Admit, order intravenous antibiotics, and consult urology or interventional radiology for drainage. Do not prescribe oral antibiotics and discharge.
lines: A glucose is controlled because the patient is usually diabetic.
Imaging is the CT that showed the gas, and it is not repeated for curiosity.
A simple pyelonephritis without gas can still go home if the patient can drink.
Gas in the kidney on CT in a diabetic patient is a necrotizing infection, usually E. coli or another gram-negative rod.
Intravenous antibiotics and drainage or nephrectomy. Oral ciprofloxacin and discharge is the miss.
miss: A three-day ciprofloxacin prescription for gas in the kidney.

source.name: StatPearls. Emphysematous Pyelonephritis.
source.says: Diabetes mellitus is found in over 90% of patients with emphysematous pyelonephritis, with mortality of 40% to 90%; care combines antimicrobial therapy with percutaneous drainage or surgical intervention.

title: Ulcer bleed orders: two lines, a type and screen, transfuse at 7
lead: Order two large-bore IVs, a type and screen, and a transfusion threshold of 7 if there is no active cardiovascular disease. Endoscopy is after resuscitation, within 24 hours.
lines: Without cardiovascular disease, transfuse when hemoglobin is under 7 g/dL.
Scope after resuscitation, generally within 24 hours. Do not scope an unstable patient.
High-risk stigmata get endoscopic therapy and a proton-pump inhibitor infusion. Active heart disease uses a higher threshold.
miss: Transfusing to a hemoglobin of 10 before the endoscopy.
diagramAlt: Ulcer bleed transfusion. No heart disease: transfuse under 7 g/dL Scope after resuscitation, within 24 h Higher threshold if active coronary disease

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Upper Gastrointestinal and Ulcer Bleeding.
source.says: For patients hospitalized with UGIB, red cell transfusion at a threshold of 7 g/dL is suggested, and endoscopy is suggested within 24 hours. Endoscopic therapy is recommended for active spurting, oozing, or nonbleeding visible vessels, followed by high-dose PPI for 3 days.

title: Variceal bleed orders: octreotide, an antibiotic, and a scope
lead: Order octreotide, an intravenous antibiotic, and urgent endoscopy. Do not order a beta blocker while the patient is in shock.
lines: Intubate before the scope if the hematemesis is massive.
Band ligation is the endoscopic plan.
The beta blocker is a discharge drug after the bleeding has stopped.
Acute variceal bleeding: a vasoactive drug such as octreotide, an intravenous antibiotic, and banding. Restrict the transfusion.
Acute variceal bleeding is treated with a vasoactive drug, an antibiotic, and endoscopic therapy. A nonselective beta blocker is prevention after hemostasis, not the treatment of shock.
miss: Starting propranolol in the resuscitation bay.
diagramAlt: Variceal bleed. Octreotide + IV antibiotic Band. Do not start a beta blocker in shock Beta blocker is secondary prevention later

source.name: AASLD Practice Guidance on risk stratification and management of portal hypertension and varices in cirrhosis.
source.says: Suspected variceal bleeding is managed with resuscitation, a conservative transfusion strategy, and prompt vasoactive therapy and antimicrobial prophylaxis, with endoscopic evaluation within 12 hours. Without TIPS, a nonselective beta blocker starts when vasoactive therapy stops.

title: New ascites: tap before you raise the diuretic
lead: Order a diagnostic tap before you increase the diuretic for new or worsened ascites. Send a cell count, albumin, and a bedside-inoculated culture.
lines: A neutrophil count of 250 or more is antibiotics now.
Albumin is ordered if you remove more than 5 liters.
A SAAG of 1.1 or more is portal hypertension and changes the differential.
miss: Doubling the spironolactone over the phone for a new tense abdomen.

source.name: AASLD Practice Guidance: Diagnosis, Evaluation, and Management of Ascites, Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis and Hepatorenal Syndrome.
source.says: A diagnostic paracentesis should be performed in all patients with new-onset ascites. A SAAG of 1.1 g/dL or more is highly suggestive of portal hypertension. IV antibiotics are started empirically, before culture results, when ascitic PMN count exceeds 250/mm3. Albumin 6-8 g per liter removed is given for paracentesis over 5 L.

title: Pancreatitis orders: fluids and a diet when the pain allows
lead: Order lactated Ringer's or a similar crystalloid and a diet as soon as the pain allows. Do not order nothing by mouth for a week.
lines: Antibiotics are not ordered for uncomplicated pancreatitis.
A rising urea or hematocrit is a reason to give more fluid, written as a reassessment.
Two of three: typical pain, lipase at least three times the upper limit, and imaging when the diagnosis is unclear. Do not trend lipase daily.
Lactated Ringer's early. Antibiotics are not routine for uncomplicated disease. A rising urea or hematocrit means the patient is still behind on fluid.
miss: A week of bowel rest and prophylactic imipenem.

source.name: American College of Gastroenterology Guidelines: Management of Acute Pancreatitis.
source.says: Acute pancreatitis is diagnosed by 2 of 3: typical pain, amylase or lipase over 3 times the upper limit, and characteristic imaging. Gallstones (40%-70%) and alcohol (25%-35%) are the most common causes. Early oral feeding is suggested in mild disease; prophylactic antibiotics are not suggested even in severe disease.

title: Jaundice means the stone may have left the gallbladder
lead: Cholecystitis with jaundice is not a simple gallbladder. Order an evaluation of the duct before you treat it as an isolated cystic-duct stone.
lines: Fever and low pressure with jaundice are a duct emergency, and antibiotics start while that evaluation is arranged.
Ultrasound of the gallbladder alone can miss the duct stone.
The gallbladder operation is still needed later. It is not the emergency drainage of a blocked duct.
Jaundice, a dilated duct, or cholangitis means the stone is no longer only in the gallbladder. That needs duct drainage, not cholecystectomy alone.
miss: Booking an elective cholecystectomy next month for a jaundiced, febrile patient.

source.name: StatPearls. Acute Cholecystitis.
source.says: Acute cholecystitis is most often caused by gallstone obstruction of the cystic duct. For appropriate surgical candidates, early laparoscopic cholecystectomy during the initial hospitalization remains the preferred approach.

more.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018: flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis.

title: Cholecystitis: surgery consult and antibiotics, not antibiotics alone
lead: Order a surgical consult for early cholecystectomy and antibiotics. Do not discharge a febrile, Murphy-positive patient on oral antibiotics as the definitive plan.
lines: Pain control and nothing by mouth until surgery is the immediate order.
Ultrasound is the image if it has not been done.
Jaundice and hypotension move the diagnosis toward the duct and a different procedure.
Jaundice means the stone may be in the duct. That is a different drainage than removing the gallbladder alone.
miss: A 7-day antibiotic prescription and a clinic appointment for biliary colic that is actually cholecystitis.

source.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018: flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis.
source.says: For Grade I, TG18 recommends early Lap-C if the patients meet the criteria of CCI ≤5 and ASA-PS ≤2. For Grade II, early Lap-C by experienced surgeons if those criteria are met; if not, Lap-C after medical treatment and/or gallbladder drainage.

more.name: StatPearls. Acute Cholecystitis.

title: Bowel obstruction: suction, fluids, and a surgery call if ischemic
lead: Order nasogastric suction and fluids for a stable obstruction. Order an immediate surgical consult if there is fever, peritonitis, or a rising lactate.
lines: Prior surgery makes adhesions likely and does not make ischemia impossible.
A closed loop is named on the CT so it is not observed.
Antiemetics are given. Opioids are not the only plan.
Adhesions after surgery are the common cause. Nasogastric suction and fluids if the patient is stable and there is no peritonitis.
miss: Observing a peritonitic obstruction overnight because the last one resolved.

source.name: Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the WSES.
source.says: Non-operative management should always be tried in adhesive small bowel obstruction unless there are signs of peritonitis, strangulation, or bowel ischemia; it includes fluid resuscitation, electrolyte correction, nutritional support, and prevention of aspiration.

more.name: StatPearls. Small Bowel Obstruction.

title: Mesenteric ischemia: CTA and a surgeon, lactate is not the gate
lead: Order CT angiography and a surgical consult when the pain is out of proportion. Do not wait for the lactate to rise.
lines: Heparin is ordered if an embolus is the working diagnosis and bleeding is not the problem.
A normal abdominal exam is written down so nobody is reassured by it.
Fluids and a lactate are ordered, and the lactate is not the permission to call.
Pain with a soft abdomen, often atrial fibrillation or low flow. Lactate rises after bowel is injured.
miss: A lactate in the morning and a surgery consult if it is high.

source.name: Acute mesenteric ischemia: updated guidelines of the World Society of Emergency Surgery.
source.says: Severe abdominal pain out of proportion to physical findings should be assumed to be acute mesenteric ischemia until disproven. CTA should be performed without delay, even with acute kidney injury. Lactate alone does not reliably separate early from irreversible ischemia.

title: Do not start a gluten-free diet the week of the biopsy
lead: If you are confirming celiac disease with a biopsy, order the patient to keep eating gluten until the biopsy. A diet started early makes the test false.
lines: Check total IgA on the lab order.
Iron is replaced if the patient is deficient, and the cause is still proved.
The diet is the treatment after the test, and the referral to a dietitian is written.
Order IgA tissue transglutaminase and a total IgA while the patient is still eating gluten. A gluten-free week before the test can make it falsely negative.
miss: Congratulating a patient for two weeks of gluten avoidance before the endoscopy.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guidelines Update: Diagnosis and Management of Celiac Disease.
source.says: EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies is recommended to confirm the diagnosis in children and adults. Case finding is recommended; in IgA deficiency, testing uses IgG-based antibodies. Treatment is a gluten-free diet aimed at intestinal healing.

title: Severe ulcerative colitis is an inpatient decision
lead: Admit severe ulcerative colitis, order a steroid, and discontinue loperamide and opioids. Order a stool study for C. difficile.
lines: The 2025 ACG update is the current practice guideline for ulcerative colitis in adults.
A systemically ill patient is assessed under that guideline rather than continued on an unchanged outpatient plan.
Admit, start an intravenous steroid, stop loperamide and opioids, and test for C. difficile. Toxic megacolon is a surgical call.
miss: Sending a systemically ill patient with ulcerative colitis home to continue the outpatient plan.
diagramAlt: Severe ulcerative colitis. Admit. IV steroid Stop loperamide and opioids C. difficile test. Megacolon: call surgery

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline Update: Ulcerative Colitis in Adults.
source.says: In acute severe UC, give methylprednisolone 60 mg/day or hydrocortisone 100 mg 3-4 times daily, test initially for C. difficile, and avoid NSAIDs, narcotics, and anticholinergic drugs. Failure of IV steroids by 3 days calls for infliximab or cyclosporine rescue.

title: Achalasia: nothing by mouth if aspirating, and a myotomy referral
lead: If the patient is aspirating, order nothing by mouth and a myotomy or dilation referral. Do not refill the proton-pump inhibitor as the treatment.
lines: Manometry is the outpatient confirmatory test if it has not been done.
Aspiration precautions are written for tonight.
Failure of LES relaxation and absent peristalsis. Bird-beak barium. Manometry confirms. Endoscopy excludes a cancer mimic.
Treatment disrupts the sphincter (dilation, myotomy). A proton-pump inhibitor does not. Aspirating patients are kept from eating until that plan is set.
miss: A higher-dose proton-pump inhibitor and a regular diet.

source.name: ACG Clinical Guidelines: Diagnosis and Management of Achalasia.
source.says: Esophageal pressure topography (high-resolution manometry) is recommended for diagnosis. Disruptive LES therapy is the treatment: laparoscopic Heller myotomy over botulinum toxin in surgical candidates, pneumatic dilation over botulinum toxin, and POEM or myotomy for type III.

title: Chronic pancreatitis enzymes are written with meals
lead: Write the enzyme with each meal and snack. Order alcohol cessation as a prescription-level instruction, not a suggestion in the last line.
lines: A glucose is on the discharge labs.
A new jaundice is an imaging order before discharge.
Pain control is a plan that is not only opioids.
Fecal elastase is low. Enzymes are taken with every meal and snack, not at bedtime alone.
Alcohol cessation is the disease-modifying step. New jaundice is imaged as cancer, not treated with more enzymes.
miss: One capsule at bedtime on the label.

source.name: StatPearls. Chronic Pancreatitis.
source.says: Pancreatic enzyme supplementation is typically taken with meals.

title: H. pylori treatment is a regimen and a test of cure
lead: Order a full eradication regimen and a test of cure. Do not order a proton-pump inhibitor alone for a positive test.
lines: For a treatment-naive patient, when susceptibility is unknown, bismuth quadruple therapy for 14 days is the preferred ACG regimen.
Rifabutin triple therapy or a potassium-competitive acid blocker dual therapy for 14 days is an alternative if there is no penicillin allergy.
Do not use a clarithromycin salvage regimen unless susceptibility to clarithromycin is confirmed.
miss: Prescribing clarithromycin again without a susceptibility result, or skipping the test of cure.
diagramAlt: H. pylori. Full eradication regimen Test of cure after antibiotics PPI alone does not eradicate

source.name: ACG Clinical Guideline: Treatment of Helicobacter pylori Infection.
source.says: For treatment-naive patients, bismuth quadruple therapy for 14 days is the preferred regimen when antibiotic susceptibility is unknown. Rifabutin triple therapy or potassium-competitive acid blocker dual therapy for 14 days is a suitable alternative without penicillin allergy. Clarithromycin or levofloxacin salvage only if susceptibility is confirmed; post-treatment test-of-cure is universal.

title: DKA orders: potassium, then insulin, then dextrose
lead: Order a potassium before the insulin. If it is under 3.5, replace it first. Add dextrose when the glucose falls and keep the insulin running until the ketoacidosis resolves.
lines: Fluids are the first line of the order set.
Bicarbonate is not a routine order.
The home SGLT2 inhibitor is held and a sick-day plan is written.
Anion-gap acidosis and ketones. If potassium is under 3.5 mmol/L, replace it before insulin, because insulin will drop the serum potassium.
Potassium is known before insulin. Insulin continues, with dextrose, until ketoacidosis resolves.
miss: Stopping the insulin drip at a glucose of 180 with a bicarbonate of 8.
diagramAlt: DKA order. Fluid first K under 3.5: replace K before insulin Keep insulin on; add dextrose as glucose falls

source.name: Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes: A Consensus Report.
source.says: With potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, potassium replacement should begin at 10 mmol/h and insulin is delayed until potassium is above 3.5 mmol/L. Once glucose is below 250 mg/dL, fluids contain 5-10% dextrose. Routine bicarbonate is not recommended. Resolution is ketones <0.6 mmol/L and pH ≥7.3 or bicarbonate ≥18 mmol/L.

title: Thyroid storm: PTU, then iodide an hour later
lead: Write the storm orders as propylthiouracil first, iodide no sooner than 1 hour later, plus a beta blocker and a glucocorticoid. Use acetaminophen, not aspirin. A Burch-Wartofsky score of 45 or higher is the threshold.
lines: Propylthiouracil is the thionamide preferred in storm because it also blocks conversion of T4 to T3.
Give iodide at least 1 hour after the thionamide. Iodide first supplies substrate for more hormone.
A score of 45 or more supports the diagnosis. A beta blocker alone is not the regimen.
miss: Giving iodide before the thionamide, or using aspirin for the fever.
diagramAlt: Thyroid storm sequence. PTU first. Iodide at least 1 hour later Beta blocker and a glucocorticoid BWPS >=45. No aspirin

source.name: StatPearls. Thyroid Storm.
source.says: An hour after administering propylthiouracil or methimazole, give SSKI; propylthiouracil is favored because it also blocks peripheral conversion of T4 to T3. Hydrocortisone is started, aspirin is avoided, and a Burch-Wartofsky score of 45 or more is more sensitive for thyroid storm.

more.name: 2016 American Thyroid Association Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism and Other Causes of Thyrotoxicosis.

title: Adrenal crisis: hydrocortisone and saline are stat
lead: Order hydrocortisone and normal saline as stat medications. Do not order a cosyntropin test as the first action.
lines: Crisis dose: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV now, then 200 mg over the next 24 hours, with saline.
Do not wait for a corticotropin stimulation test. Recommendation 4.1 treats the unstable patient first.
After recovery, adult maintenance is hydrocortisone 15 to 25 mg a day in divided doses plus fludrocortisone about 0.1 mg.
Send the patient out with stress-dose teaching and a parenteral glucocorticoid for the next emergency.
miss: Holding the glucocorticoid until a stimulation test is finished in an unstable patient.

source.name: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. Diagnosis and Treatment of Primary Adrenal Insufficiency.
source.says: Suspected adrenal crisis is treated with an immediate parenteral injection of 100 mg hydrocortisone, fluid resuscitation, and 200 mg hydrocortisone over 24 hours, before diagnostic results are available. Adult maintenance is hydrocortisone 15-25 mg/day in two to three doses with once-daily fludrocortisone (median 0.1 mg), plus a steroid emergency card.

title: Pheochromocytoma preparation is blockade plus salt and volume
lead: The preoperative orders show an alpha blocker already in place and volume restored. A beta blocker is not the first preoperative drug.
lines: Screen with plasma free metanephrines or urinary fractionated metanephrines. A positive result is followed up, not ignored.
Every patient with a functional tumor gets preoperative blockade before surgery.
Preparation includes a high-sodium diet and a high fluid intake so the blood pressure does not collapse after the tumor is removed.
Block the tumor before incision and load salt and volume so the pressure does not collapse after removal.
miss: Taking a functional pheochromocytoma to surgery without preoperative blockade and volume preparation.

source.name: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. Pheochromocytoma and Paraganglioma.
source.says: Initial biochemical testing should include plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines, and all positive results require follow-up. All patients with functional tumors should undergo preoperative blockade, with a high-sodium diet and fluid intake to prevent postoperative hypotension.

title: Pregnancy hypertension at 140/90 is a treatment order
lead: For chronic hypertension in pregnancy, order treatment at 140/90 rather than waiting for 160/110. ACE inhibitors and ARBs are not on the list.
lines: Home pressures are ordered, not a single clinic number.
Aspirin prevention is a different order and does not treat today's severe pressure.
Treat at 140/90. Labetalol and nifedipine are the usual agents. Stop ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and statins.
This is a threshold to treat, not proof that lower is always better. Severe-range pressures are a separate emergency.
miss: Continuing lisinopril and observing until the pressure is severe.
diagramAlt: Blood pressure in pregnancy. Chronic HTN: treat at 140/90 Severe: 160 or 110, treat within minutes Magnesium prevents seizures. It is not the BP drug

source.name: ACOG Practice Advisory. Clinical Guidance for the Integration of the Findings of the Chronic Hypertension and Pregnancy (CHAP) Study.
source.says: ACOG recommends using 140/90 as the threshold for initiation or titration of medical therapy for chronic hypertension in pregnancy, rather than the previously recommended threshold of 160/110. The CHAP study used a threshold for treatment and did not establish a goal blood pressure.

title: Severe pregnancy hypertension is treated within the hour
lead: Order an intravenous or immediate-release oral antihypertensive for a sustained pressure of 160 or 110, and order magnesium for seizure prevention. Do not wait for labs.
lines: Recheck the pressure on a schedule after the dose.
The goal is not a normal pressure of 110. Overcorrection harms the placenta.
Postpartum patients get the same order. Discharge does not end the risk.
Sustained systolic pressure of 160 or diastolic of 110 is treated promptly, with a target to bring it out of the severe range, not down to 110 systolic.
miss: Waiting for the preeclampsia labs before the first dose of labetalol.
diagramAlt: Blood pressure in pregnancy. Chronic HTN: treat at 140/90 Severe: 160 or 110, treat within minutes Magnesium prevents seizures. It is not the BP drug

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222. Gestational Hypertension and Preeclampsia (reaffirmed 2026).
source.says: Antihypertensive treatment should be initiated expeditiously for acute-onset severe hypertension (systolic 160 mm Hg or more or diastolic 110 mm Hg or more) confirmed as persistent for 15 minutes or more, as soon as reasonably possible. Magnesium sulfate should be used for the prevention and treatment of seizures in preeclampsia with severe features or eclampsia.

more.name: ACOG. Acute Hypertension in Pregnancy and Postpartum Algorithm (IV labetalol, IV hydralazine, or immediate-release oral nifedipine; give with magnesium sulfate).

title: Aspirin for preeclampsia is ordered after 12 weeks in high-risk patients
lead: Order 81 mg of aspirin after 12 weeks for a high-risk patient, and do not order it as the treatment of a pressure that is already severe.
lines: The high-risk list is prior preeclampsia, multiples, chronic hypertension, diabetes, kidney disease, or autoimmune disease.
Start it at the visit you identify the risk, not at 34 weeks.
The severe-pressure order is a different drug.
Aspirin does not treat a pressure of 170. That pressure gets an antihypertensive and, if severe features are present, magnesium.
miss: Starting aspirin at the delivery admission for a pressure of 180.

source.name: USPSTF. Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: Preventive Medication.
source.says: Low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) is recommended after 12 weeks of gestation for persons at high risk for preeclampsia: history of preeclampsia, multifetal gestation, kidney disease, autoimmune disease, type 1 or type 2 diabetes, or chronic hypertension.

title: Ectopic: surgery if unstable, methotrexate only if every criterion is met
lead: Order the operating room for an unstable ectopic pregnancy. Order methotrexate only if the patient is stable, the hCG is in range, and follow-up is certain.
lines: A type and screen is on the unstable patient's orders.
Rh immunoglobulin is ordered if the patient is Rh negative.
A discharge on methotrexate includes the day of the next hCG.
A ruptured or unstable ectopic pregnancy is managed surgically. Methotrexate is reserved for a stable patient who meets criteria and can be followed.
Give anti-D immunoglobulin if the patient is Rh-negative. An empty uterus with a positive test and pain is not a threatened miscarriage until the tube is cleared.
miss: Methotrexate and a discharge for a dizzy patient with a positive pregnancy test.
diagramAlt: Ectopic pregnancy. Shock or rupture: operating room Methotrexate only if stable and follow-up is sure Rh-negative: give anti-D

source.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 193. Tubal Ectopic Pregnancy (reaffirmed 2025).
source.says: Most tubal ectopic pregnancies detected early can be treated with minimally invasive surgery or with methotrexate. A tubal ectopic pregnancy in an unstable patient is a medical emergency that requires prompt surgical intervention.

title: Abruption orders are blood and a fetal monitor
lead: Order blood products, a fetal monitor, and large-bore access. Do not order a digital cervical exam.
lines: A fibrinogen is on the labs.
The obstetric team is called when the diagnosis is suspected.
Pain control is ordered and does not delay resuscitation.
Painful bleeding and a uterus that does not relax. Blood can be concealed. Fibrinogen falls and can be the first coagulation test to move.
Resuscitate, monitor the fetus, and decide on delivery. Do not perform a digital exam until previa is excluded.
miss: A cervical check as the first order.

source.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 63. Antepartum Haemorrhage.
source.says: If placenta praevia is possible, digital vaginal examination should not be performed until ultrasound has excluded it. With abruption and fetal death, coagulopathy and hypovolaemic shock are not uncommon; in major haemorrhage, send a coagulation screen and cross-match 4 units of blood.

title: Previa orders: no digital exam, ultrasound, and a cesarean plan
lead: Order pelvic rest, an ultrasound, and a cesarean plan if the placenta covers the cervix. Write no digital exam.
lines: A prior cesarean plus previa triggers an accreta plan at a capable hospital.
The acute bleed gets the same blood-bank orders as any maternal hemorrhage.
An outpatient bleed that has stopped still leaves with precautions and a dated delivery plan.
miss: An induction order for a complete previa.

source.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 27a. Placenta Praevia and Placenta Accreta Spectrum.
source.says: A placenta is recorded as praevia if it covers the internal os, partially or completely. Placenta praevia carries a high risk of emergency caesarean birth and haemorrhage, so birth is arranged in a unit with blood transfusion and critical care. A previous caesarean with a low-lying placenta or praevia means high risk of placenta accreta spectrum.

title: Gestational diabetes discharge watches the newborn and rescreens the mother
lead: Order an early feed and a glucose check for the newborn, and a postpartum diabetes test for the mother. Insulin, if used, is not automatically continued at the pregnancy dose.
lines: After birth, the infant is observed. Maternal glucose has been the fetal fuel.
The mother is retested for diabetes postpartum. Pregnancy treatment is not the end of the diagnosis.
Maternal glucose crosses the placenta and maternal insulin does not. The newborn is hyperinsulinemic, so feed early and check a glucose.
miss: Skipping the postpartum glucose retest, or not checking the newborn for hypoglycemia.
diagramAlt: Infant of a diabetic mother. Glucose crosses. Insulin does not Baby is hyperinsulinemic and can be hypoglycemic Feed early. Check a glucose

source.name: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. 15. Management of Diabetes in Pregnancy.
source.says: Lifestyle behavior change may suffice for many with GDM; insulin is the preferred agent for GDM, and no human insulin has been shown to cross the placenta. Individuals with recent GDM are screened at 4-12 weeks postpartum with a 75-g OGTT.

more.name: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 190. Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.

title: Ask about PDE-5 inhibitors before the first nitroglycerin
lead: The chest-pain order set includes a question about PDE-5 inhibitors before nitroglycerin is given. If the answer is yes, the nitrate is not given.
lines: The ECG and aspirin are still ordered.
Document the time of the last dose if you know it.
Sildenafil and a nitrate together can drop systolic pressure profoundly. Ask before the first spray.
miss: Giving the nitrate because the protocol says so.

source.name: 2025 ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes.
source.says: Nitrates should not be administered after recent PDE5 inhibitor use. Avoid nitrates or nitroglycerin within 12 hours of avanafil, 24 hours of sildenafil or vardenafil, or 48 hours of tadalafil.

title: BPH retention is a catheter, not a sample of tamsulosin
lead: Acute urinary retention gets a catheter and a recorded residual. An alpha blocker is started after the bladder is empty, not instead of emptying it.
lines: A creatinine is ordered if retention was prolonged.
A nodule is not attributed to hyperplasia.
Finasteride is not the drug that empties the bladder tonight.
miss: A tamsulosin prescription and no catheter for a painful full bladder.
diagramAlt: BPH drugs. Alpha blocker: days 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor: months, large gland Retention tonight: catheter, not finasteride

source.name: StatPearls. Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
source.says: The development of BPH is characterized by stromal and epithelial cell proliferation in the prostate transition zone, which surrounds the urethra.

more.name: AUA guideline. Management of lower urinary tract symptoms attributed to benign prostatic hyperplasia (2021, amended 2023).

title: Acute scrotal pain is not a morning ultrasound
lead: Consent and imaging for acute scrotal pain happen now. Ultrasound is the first-line test, and a next-morning slot is a delay.
lines: Overlapping causes make this a diagnostic emergency, not a routine scrotal complaint.
Ultrasound can diagnose most acute scrotal disorders promptly.
Document the time the pain started and the time the imaging was ordered.
miss: An ultrasound order for 8 a.m. and a regular diet.

source.name: ACR Appropriateness Criteria. Acute Onset of Scrotal Pain (Without Trauma, Without Antecedent Mass).
source.says: Acute scrotum is a medical emergency that requires prompt accurate diagnosis. Overlapping presentations make diagnosis a challenge, and ultrasound is the established first-line imaging modality for acute scrotal disease.

title: Ovarian torsion: surgical consent even when Doppler shows flow
lead: Order surgical evaluation for suspected ovarian torsion regardless of a Doppler report that shows flow. Order a pregnancy test.
lines: Nothing by mouth and consent are written.
Pain control is ordered.
An ectopic pregnancy remains on the differential until the test returns.
The ovary has a dual blood supply, so Doppler flow can be present in a twisted ovary.
Sudden adnexal pain with a cyst goes to surgery. A pregnancy test is done because ectopic pregnancy is the other emergency.
miss: Cancelling the surgical consult because the report said flow was present.

source.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 783. Adnexal Torsion in Adolescents.
source.says: If ovarian torsion is suspected, timely diagnostic laparoscopy is indicated to preserve ovarian function. No clinical or imaging criteria confirm torsion preoperatively, and Doppler flow alone should not guide decisions. Detorsion with preservation of the adnexa is recommended regardless of the appearance of the ovary.

more.name: StatPearls. Ovarian Torsion (dual ovarian blood supply).

title: Pelvic inflammatory disease: treat the partner in the note
lead: The discharge names the partner treatment and the return precautions for worsening pain. A pregnancy test is resulted before the drug.
lines: Treat the patient and arrange treatment of sex partners. A prescription for one person is not the regimen.
Cervical motion tenderness is the examination finding that starts that guideline, not a normal Pap smear.
Treat gonorrhea and chlamydia in the patient, and treat the partner in the same plan.
miss: Treating pelvic inflammatory disease without a plan for the partner.
diagramAlt: PID coverage. Cover gonorrhea and chlamydia Treat the partner Abscess that fails antibiotics: drain

source.name: CDC Sexually Transmitted Infections Treatment Guidelines, 2021. Pelvic Inflammatory Disease.
source.says: All PID regimens should be effective against N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis, because negative endocervical screening does not rule out upper tract infection. Partners from the 60 days before symptom onset should be evaluated, tested, and presumptively treated for chlamydia and gonorrhea, regardless of the PID etiology.

title: Postmenopausal bleeding is a biopsy order, not a repeat Pap
lead: Order an endometrial biopsy or a referral that will do one. Do not order a repeat Pap smear as the evaluation.
lines: Ultrasound stripe thickness can triage some patients and does not replace a biopsy when bleeding is persistent.
Stop unopposed estrogen if that is the cause, and still evaluate.
Anticoagulation is not an adequate explanation by itself.
Any bleeding after menopause is sampled. A Pap smear does not reach the endometrium.
miss: A repeat Pap smear in a year.
diagramAlt: Postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy, not a repeat Pap Unopposed estrogen is the setup A thin stripe does not erase persistent bleeding

source.name: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 734. The Role of Transvaginal Ultrasonography in Evaluating the Endometrium of Women With Postmenopausal Bleeding.
source.says: Transvaginal ultrasonography is a reasonable alternative to endometrial sampling as a first approach in an initial episode of bleeding; an endometrial thickness of 4 mm or less has a greater than 99% negative predictive value. If blind sampling does not reveal hyperplasia or malignancy, further testing such as hysteroscopy with D&C is warranted for persistent or recurrent bleeding.

title: Hyperthyroidism in pregnancy: the drug matches the trimester
lead: Order propylthiouracil in the first trimester and a plan to change to methimazole afterward. Do not order radioactive iodine.
lines: If an antithyroid drug is required in the first trimester, the ATA specifies propylthiouracil.
Women on methimazole who become pregnant are switched early in the first trimester when a drug is still required.
The trimester, not a preference for one drug in every month, chooses the agent.
miss: Continuing methimazole through the first trimester when an antithyroid drug is still required.
diagramAlt: Antithyroid drug by trimester. First trimester: propylthiouracil After that: methimazole No radioactive iodine in pregnancy

source.name: 2017 Guidelines of the American Thyroid Association for the Diagnosis and Management of Thyroid Disease During Pregnancy and the Postpartum.
source.says: The revised guidelines for the management of thyroid disease in pregnancy include recommendations regarding the interpretation of thyroid function tests in pregnancy, thyrotoxicosis in pregnancy, fetal and neonatal considerations, and thyroid disease and lactation.

more.name: 2016 ATA Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism and Other Causes of Thyrotoxicosis.

title: A pituitary mass with a TSH of 80 is thyroid hormone, not a surgical date
lead: Order thyroid hormone and a repeat image for pituitary enlargement caused by severe hypothyroidism. Do not book surgery first.
lines: A prolactin is interpreted in light of the TSH.
The surgical referral is cancelled or delayed until the thyroid is replaced.
The patient is warned that the mass can shrink.
Severe primary hypothyroidism raises TRH, which can raise prolactin and enlarge the pituitary. That enlargement can be hyperplasia.
Replace thyroid hormone and reimage. A prolactin only modestly high with a large mass is stalk effect, not an indication for immediate surgery.
miss: A transsphenoidal date for a patient whose TSH has not been checked.

source.name: StatPearls. Pituitary Hyperplasia in Primary Hypothyroidism.
source.says: Pituitary hyperplasia can cause features of hypothyroidism, hyperprolactinemia, and even visual field defects if the gland compresses the optic chiasm. Recognition of this entity is important, as the primary modality of treatment is thyroid hormone replacement rather than surgery.

title: Sepsis orders are lactate, cultures, drug, and a fluid with a reassessment
lead: Order a lactate, cultures if they will not delay the drug, a broad antibiotic, and crystalloid if the pressure is low or the lactate is at least 4. Order a blood pressure reassessment, not an unmeasured bolus.
lines: A vasopressor is ordered if the pressure stays low, aimed at a mean pressure of 65.
The suspected source is named so the drug matches it.
A virus swab does not replace the antibiotic.
Lactate of at least 4 mmol/L or hypotension after the infection is recognized: at least 30 mL/kg crystalloid, then reassess.
miss: One liter of fluid and a lactate in the morning.
diagramAlt: Sepsis hypoperfusion. Lactate, cultures, broad antibiotic At least 30 mL/kg crystalloid if hypoperfused Norepinephrine to MAP 65 if still hypotensive

source.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2026.
source.says: For sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or septic shock, at least 30 mL/kg of IV crystalloid in the first 3 hours is suggested. Blood cultures are collected as soon as possible, ideally before antimicrobials; antimicrobials for possible septic shock or probable sepsis are given immediately, ideally within 1 hour; the initial MAP target is 65 mm Hg.

more.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026, Intensive Care Medicine full text.

title: Anaphylaxis: epinephrine in the thigh, and a period of watching
lead: Order intramuscular epinephrine in the mid-outer thigh and a period of observation. Do not order diphenhydramine as the only drug.
lines: Epinephrine is 0.01 mg/kg, to a maximum of 0.3 mg in children and teenagers and 0.5 mg in adults.
Give epinephrine at the first sign of suspected anaphylaxis.
Draw an acute tryptase as early as possible, ideally within 2 hours of symptom onset. A later baseline is the comparison.
A tryptase under the laboratory cutoff does not exclude anaphylaxis. Many confirmed reactions never cross that line.
miss: Treating anaphylaxis with an antihistamine and quoting a flat 0.3 mg dose for every adult.
diagramAlt: Anaphylaxis dose. Adult: 0.3–0.5 mg of 1 mg/mL IM Mid-outer thigh. Repeat in 5–15 min Watch. Antihistamine is not the treatment

source.name: World Allergy Organization Anaphylaxis Guidance 2020.
source.says: Intramuscular epinephrine is the first-line drug for anaphylaxis. The healthcare-professional dose is 0.01 mg/kg, to a maximum total dose of 0.5 mg, given intramuscularly in the mid-anterolateral thigh and repeated every 5-15 minutes if symptoms are refractory.

more.name: Anaphylaxis: a 2023 practice parameter update.

title: Carbon monoxide: 100% oxygen now, and the cohabitants
lead: Order 100% oxygen and a carboxyhemoglobin. Ask who else was in the house and order them evaluated if they share the exposure.
lines: Do not clear the patient with a standard pulse oximeter reading. The policy is about measured carboxyhemoglobin and the hyperbaric decision.
Anyone who shared the exposure is assessed. A normal-appearing cohabitant is not proof the air was safe.
Hyperbaric selection follows the policy. A numeric affinity ratio is not the indication.
miss: Discharging a symptomatic patient because the pulse oximeter read normal.
diagramAlt: Carbon monoxide. PaO2 and pulse ox can look normal Content is low. Curve shifts left 100% oxygen now. Whole household

source.name: ACEP Clinical Policy. A Critical Issue in the Management of Adult Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department With Acute Carbon Monoxide Poisoning.
source.says: In symptomatic carbon monoxide poisoning, selected patients may benefit from hyperbaric oxygen treatment based on severity of symptoms and availability (distance and time).

more.name: ACEP clinical policy, Ann Emerg Med 2025 full text.

title: Acetaminophen: start the antidote and plot the time
lead: Order N-acetylcysteine when the level is toxic or the time of a large ingestion is unknown. Write the time of ingestion on the order so the nomogram is used correctly.
lines: On the treatment line, 150 micrograms per mL at 4 hours is the level that starts acetylcysteine.
Give acetylcysteine within 8 hours of a single acute ingestion when that line is crossed.
The 2023 consensus uses a revised Rumack-Matthew nomogram for a presentation from 4 to 24 hours. A 2-hour level does not clear the patient.
A normal early ALT is not a reason to withhold the antidote.
miss: Waiting past 8 hours, or trusting a 2-hour level, before starting acetylcysteine.
diagramAlt: Acetaminophen antidote. NAPQI uses up glutathione NAC if level is toxic or time is unknown Normal ALT at 2 hours does not clear it

source.name: Management of Acetaminophen Poisoning in the US and Canada: A Consensus Statement.
source.says: The consensus defines acute ingestion as a presentation from 4 to 24 hours after overdose began and uses a revised Rumack-Matthew nomogram, with a high-risk ingestion line in place of the term massive ingestion.

title: Naloxone is an order with a recheck, not a single dose and a goodbye
lead: Order naloxone and an observation period long enough for the opioid you suspect. A long-acting opioid gets a longer watch or an infusion.
lines: Support ventilation first if the patient is not breathing. Naloxone does not replace that.
Intravenous naloxone in the AHA poisoning guidance is 0.2 to 2 mg. FDA-labeled nasal spray is 4 mg. Repeat every 2 to 3 minutes.
Titrate to breathing and airway reflexes. A long-acting opioid needs a longer watch because depression returns.
A benzodiazepine taken with the opioid does not delay the naloxone.
miss: One dose of naloxone and a discharge as soon as the patient wakes.
diagramAlt: Naloxone wears off. Opioid half-life is often longer Observe or infuse Methadone and fentanyl outlast one dose

source.name: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC. Part 10: Adult and Pediatric Special Circumstances of Resuscitation.
source.says: An opioid antagonist such as naloxone should be given to people with respiratory arrest from suspected opioid overdose. In cardiac arrest from presumed opioid overdose, an opioid antagonist may be reasonable if high-quality CPR is not interrupted.

title: Do not order flumazenil on a daily benzodiazepine user
lead: Order airway support. Do not order flumazenil for a patient who takes a benzodiazepine every day.
lines: A benzodiazepine alone rarely stops breathing the way an opioid does.
Do not give flumazenil to a daily user or in a mixed overdose. It can precipitate a seizure.
If an opioid may be on board, give naloxone. The 2023 update treats naloxone as the safer reversal.
Support the airway while you sort out the mix.
miss: Waking a daily benzodiazepine user with flumazenil and causing a seizure.

source.name: StatPearls. Benzodiazepine Toxicity.
source.says: Flumazenil can precipitate acute withdrawal in those with chronic benzodiazepine dependence; given to a dependent patient it can lower the seizure threshold and cause life-threatening seizures.

more.name: 2023 AHA Focused Update on the Management of Patients With Cardiac Arrest or Life-Threatening Toxicity Due to Poisoning.

title: Alcohol withdrawal: a scored benzodiazepine protocol and thiamine first
lead: Order a symptom-triggered benzodiazepine protocol and thiamine before any glucose. Do not order haloperidol as the only withdrawal drug.
lines: A monitored bed is ordered for delirium tremens.
The last drink time is written so the team expects the late delirium.
Electrolytes, especially magnesium, are on the labs.
Tremor at about 6–24 hours, seizures at 12–48 hours, delirium tremens at 48–72 hours. Use a symptom-triggered benzodiazepine.
Thiamine before any glucose. An antipsychotic alone does not prevent the seizure. Do not discharge a patient still scoring in the severe range.
miss: Haloperidol every six hours and a glucose infusion with no thiamine.
diagramAlt: Alcohol withdrawal orders. Thiamine before glucose Benzodiazepine titrated to symptoms Haloperidol alone does not stop the seizure

source.name: The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management.
source.says: Symptom-triggered treatment by trained staff is the preferred benzodiazepine dosing method with continuous monitoring, and front loading is recommended for patients at high risk of severe withdrawal. Thiamine should be provided to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy, and antipsychotics are not recommended as monotherapy.

title: Rhabdomyolysis: a fluid rate and a repeat potassium
lead: Order intravenous fluids at a stated rate and a repeat potassium. Order a microscope look at the urine, not only the dipstick.
lines: A compartment pressure or a surgical consult is ordered for a tight limb.
The statin is held on the order.
The creatine kinase is trended, not used as a one-time curiosity.
Intravenous fluid at a defined rate and a repeat potassium. A tight compartment is opened. Stop the statin.
miss: A single bag of saline and no repeat potassium.
diagramAlt: Rhabdomyolysis labs. Dipstick blood, no RBCs on microscope CK in the thousands. K can kill first IV fluid. Open a tight compartment

source.name: StatPearls. Rhabdomyolysis.
source.says: Management aims to maintain adequate fluid resuscitation and prevent AKI, after identifying and removing the cause. Muscle breakdown releases potassium, causing hyperkalemia, and microscopy separates myoglobinuria from hemoglobinuria by the absence of red blood cells.

title: Malignant hyperthermia: stop the gas and give dantrolene
lead: The intraoperative order is to stop the volatile agent, hyperventilate with 100% oxygen, and give dantrolene. Cooling is ordered with it.
lines: The dantrolene dose is repeated as the protocol says. One vial is not the whole treatment.
Potassium and urine output are ordered because muscle is dying.
The team is told this is not light anesthesia.
This is not neuroleptic malignant syndrome.
miss: Increasing the vaporizer and ordering acetaminophen.
diagramAlt: Malignant hyperthermia. Volatile agent or succinylcholine Rising CO2, then heat and rigidity Stop the gas. Dantrolene. 100% oxygen

source.name: European Malignant Hyperthermia Group. Recognising and managing a malignant hyperthermia crisis (v2024).
source.says: Stop all trigger agents, hyperventilate with 100% oxygen at high flow, and call for help. Give dantrolene 2-2.5 mg/kg IV, repeated every 10 minutes. Inappropriately elevated CO2 production is an early sign, and trigger agents are volatile anaesthetics and succinylcholine.

more.name: EMHG 2024 guideline, Br J Anaesth 2025;134:221-223.

title: Fat embolism: oxygen and fix the fracture
lead: Order oxygen and early fracture fixation. Do not order heparin as the specific treatment of fat embolism.
lines: A chest finding and petechiae are documented.
A true venous clot is still considered and is a separate order.
The orthopedic team is called for the fixation, which is the source control.
Support the lungs and fix the fracture. Heparin is not the specific treatment. A venous thrombus is a separate question.
miss: A heparin drip as the only order and a delayed fixation.

source.name: StatPearls. Fat Embolism and Fat Embolism Syndrome.
source.says: Fat embolism typically manifests 24 to 72 hours after the initial insult. Once FES develops, supportive care is the mainstay of treatment, early fixation of long-bone fractures is recommended, and heparin has no proven clinical benefit.

title: Delirium: stop diphenhydramine and search the bladder
lead: Order a stop to anticholinergic drugs, a bladder scan, and a search for infection. Do not order a benzodiazepine for a non-withdrawal delirium.
lines: Glasses and hearing aids are an order, not a courtesy.
Restraints are not the first safety order.
The family is asked what the patient was like last week.
Stop benzodiazepines and strong anticholinergics, including diphenhydramine, when they contributed to the admission.
Benzodiazepines are for alcohol or benzodiazepine withdrawal, not for ordinary delirium. Bladder scan before a new antipsychotic.
miss: Lorazepam around the clock and a Foley catheter for convenience.
diagramAlt: Delirium, first orders. Stop diphenhydramine and benzodiazepines Bladder scan. Look for infection Benzo only for alcohol or benzo withdrawal

source.name: American Geriatrics Society 2023 Updated AGS Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults.
source.says: Anticholinergics, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, and Z-drugs: avoid in older adults with or at high risk of delirium because of the potential of inducing or worsening delirium. First-generation antihistamines such as diphenhydramine are highly anticholinergic, with a risk of confusion.

title: A Beers list drug is removed at discharge if it caused the admission
lead: If a benzodiazepine, a strong anticholinergic, or sliding-scale insulin alone contributed to the admission, take it off the discharge list.
lines: The 2023 Beers list flags benzodiazepines, strong anticholinergics including diphenhydramine, and sliding-scale insulin used alone.
If one of those drugs caused the fall, the delirium, or the hypoglycemia, do not restart it at discharge.
Replace the job it was doing: a non-benzodiazepine sleep plan, a non-anticholinergic pain plan, or a basal insulin plan.
A home medication list is not an order to resume the offending drug.
miss: Restarting the admission-causing benzodiazepine because it is on the home list.
diagramAlt: Beers drugs that cause admissions. Benzodiazepines for sleep or anxiety Strong anticholinergics, including diphenhydramine Sliding-scale insulin used alone

source.name: American Geriatrics Society 2023 Updated AGS Beers Criteria for Potentially Inappropriate Medication Use in Older Adults.
source.says: Benzodiazepines: avoid. First-generation antihistamines, including diphenhydramine: highly anticholinergic, avoid. Sliding-scale insulin: higher risk of hypoglycemia without improvement in hyperglycemia management regardless of care setting; avoid regimens with only short- or rapid-acting insulin and no basal insulin.

title: Opioid start: immediate release, a low dose, and naloxone if the risk is high
lead: If an opioid is started, order immediate release, the lowest effective dose, and naloxone if the patient has overdose risk. Do not start an extended-release opioid.
lines: A nonopioid is ordered for many acute pains and is not skipped.
The duration is days, written as a number.
Benzodiazepines are not combined without a reason you would defend.
Start immediate-release opioid at the lowest dose, for days, not an extended-release product. Offer naloxone if risk is high.
miss: A long-acting opioid as the first prescription after an injury.
diagramAlt: Starting an opioid. Immediate release, lowest dose Not an extended-release first opioid Offer naloxone if overdose risk is high

source.name: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain, United States, 2022.
source.says: When starting opioid therapy for acute, subacute, or chronic pain, clinicians should prescribe immediate-release opioids instead of extended-release and long-acting opioids. For opioid-naive patients, prescribe the lowest effective dosage. Clinicians should offer naloxone when prescribing opioids, particularly to patients at increased risk for overdose.

title: A handoff uses I-PASS out loud
lead: The handoff order of information is illness severity, a patient summary, the action list, situational awareness, and a synthesis by the receiver.
lines: Illness severity is one word the next clinician can use at 3 a.m.
A written note that was not spoken is not a handoff.
Illness severity, patient summary, action list with a time, a contingency, and the receiver saying the plan back.
A copied problem list with no watch item is not a handoff. The verbal read-back still happens when a note exists.
miss: A signed-out list with no severity and no read-back.
diagramAlt: I-PASS. Illness severity Summary, action list, contingency Receiver says the plan back

source.name: Starmer AJ et al. Changes in medical errors after implementation of a handoff program (I-PASS). N Engl J Med.
source.says: The intervention included a mnemonic to standardize oral and written handoffs and handoff and communication training. The medical-error rate decreased by 23% (24.5 vs. 18.8 per 100 admissions), and preventable adverse events decreased by 30% (4.7 vs. 3.3 per 100 admissions).

title: A positive stool test orders a colonoscopy
lead: A positive stool-based colorectal test is followed by colonoscopy. Do not order a repeat stool test.
lines: The patient is told that before the first stool kit.
Average-risk screening still starts at 45.
Iron deficiency is a diagnostic colonoscopy, not a screening interval.
Average-risk screening starts at 45 and continues through 75. A positive stool test is a colonoscopy, not another card.
A first-degree relative with cancer before 60 starts earlier. Ages 76–85 are selective.
miss: Repeating the stool card after a positive result.
diagramAlt: Positive stool test. Colonoscopy next, not another card Average risk starts at 45 Iron deficiency is diagnostic, not screening

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal Cancer: Screening.
source.says: Positive results on stool-based screening tests require follow-up with colonoscopy for the screening benefits to be achieved. The USPSTF expanded the recommended ages for colorectal cancer screening to 45 to 75 years.

title: A breast lump is a diagnostic order, not the next screening date
lead: A palpable breast mass is a diagnostic imaging order now. It is not postponed until the next biennial mammogram.
lines: Screening mammography is for people without that symptom.
