Age 40 to 74 is the screening window. A mass at any age in that window is still diagnostic.
Screening schedules do not apply to a palpable mass. Diagnostic imaging is ordered.
miss: Scheduling a screening mammogram in eight months for a new lump.
diagramAlt: Lump versus screen. A mass is diagnostic imaging now Screen: every other year, 40 through 74 Age 75+: not an automatic order

source.name: USPSTF. Breast Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years. These recommendations do not apply to persons who have a genetic marker or syndrome associated with a high risk of breast cancer, a history of high-dose radiation therapy to the chest at a young age, or previous breast cancer.

title: Document the lung-screening conversation before the scan
lead: Before the first low-dose CT, document the shared decision: the benefit, the false positives, and that the patient still smokes or quit within 15 years.
lines: Confirm eligibility before the order: age 50–80, at least 20 pack-years, and either still smoking or quit less than 15 years ago.
Shared decision-making is documented before the initial low-dose CT. Symptoms convert the order from screening to diagnosis.
Stop after 15 smoke-free years, at age 81, or when treatment of a found cancer would not help.
A symptomatic cough, hemoptysis, or weight loss is a diagnostic CT, not a screening code.
miss: Ordering the scan with no note that the patient agreed after hearing the harms.
diagramAlt: Stop the yearly lung CT. Eligible: 50–80, ≥20 pack-years Stop 15 years after quitting Stop at age 81, or if too ill to benefit

source.name: USPSTF. Lung Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF recommends annual screening for lung cancer with low-dose CT in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years. The decision to undertake screening should involve a discussion of its potential benefits, limitations, and harms.

title: Stop cervical screening at 65 only if the prior tests were adequate
lead: You may stop cervical screening at 65 only when the recent tests were adequate and negative. A patient with no records is not stopped.
lines: HPV testing alone is not the order before age 30.
Bleeding after sex is examined now even if the last test was normal.
Vaccination does not delete the schedule.
Types 16 and 18 cause most cervical cancers. Screening starts at 21, not at coitarche.
Ages 21–29: cytology every 3 years, not HPV testing alone. Ages 30–65: cytology every 3 years, HPV every 5, or cotesting every 5. Stop at 65 only if prior tests were adequate.
miss: Stopping screening at 65 because the patient cannot remember her last Pap.
diagramAlt: Cervical screening intervals. Start at 21, not at first sex 21–29: cytology every 3 years 30–65: cytology q3, HPV q5, or both q5

source.name: USPSTF. Cervical Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF recommends against screening for cervical cancer in women older than 65 years who have had adequate prior screening and are not otherwise at high risk for cervical cancer.

title: Do not order HPV testing alone before age 30
lead: Ages 21 to 29 are cytology every 3 years. Do not order high-risk HPV testing alone in that age band.
lines: A yearly Pap is not the recommendation.
A visible cervical lesion is a biopsy, not a screening interval.
Primary HPV testing is not the strategy before age 30. Cytology every 3 years is.
Ages 30–65 may use HPV every 5 years. Stop at 65 only when recent tests were adequate and negative. Postcoital bleeding is examined now.
miss: An HPV-only order for a 24-year-old.
diagramAlt: Cervical screening intervals. Start at 21, not at first sex 21–29: cytology every 3 years 30–65: cytology q3, HPV q5, or both q5

source.name: USPSTF. Cervical Cancer: Screening.
source.says: Screening every 3 years with cervical cytology alone in women aged 21 to 29 years. For women aged 30 to 65 years, every 3 years with cytology alone, every 5 years with hrHPV testing alone, or every 5 years with cotesting. False-positive rates are higher among women younger than 30 years because of transient HPV infection.

title: Age 75 mammography is a decision, not an automatic order
lead: At 75 and older, do not order mammography automatically. The USPSTF found the evidence insufficient, so you decide with the patient.
lines: Biennial mammography is recommended from 40 through 74. Age 75 and older is an I statement: evidence is insufficient for a routine order.
Decide from life expectancy and whether the patient would treat a cancer the scan might find.
A palpable mass is diagnostic imaging now, at any age, including over 75.
Supplemental ultrasound for dense breasts is not a required add-on. That is also an I statement.
miss: A standing yearly mammogram order with no stop date for an 82-year-old.
diagramAlt: Lump versus screen. A mass is diagnostic imaging now Screen: every other year, 40 through 74 Age 75+: not an automatic order

source.name: USPSTF. Breast Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF concludes that the current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening mammography in women 75 years or older.

title: Colon screening after 75 is selective
lead: From 76 to 85, colorectal screening is selective. It is not ordered for a patient whose other illnesses will not allow a benefit.
lines: Average-risk screening is recommended through age 75. Ages 76–85 are selective (a C recommendation).
Select using screening history, comorbidity, and whether the patient could tolerate treatment of a found cancer.
Stop after 85. A positive stool test at any age in this discussion is still a colonoscopy, not another card.
Retrieve the date of the last complete colonoscopy before you order another.
miss: Ordering a first colonoscopy at 84 for a patient in hospice-level heart failure.
diagramAlt: Positive stool test. Colonoscopy next, not another card Average risk starts at 45 Iron deficiency is diagnostic, not screening

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians selectively offer screening for colorectal cancer in adults aged 76 to 85 years. Evidence indicates that the net benefit of screening all persons in this age group is small.

title: An early colon cancer in the family moves the start age
lead: A first-degree relative with colorectal cancer before 60, or two relatives at any age, starts screening earlier than 45. Order that earlier plan.
lines: Family history of early colorectal cancer changes the start age and often the test. The average-risk age of 45 does not apply.
A common plan is to begin 10 years before that relative's age at diagnosis, and to use colonoscopy rather than a stool kit alone.
One relative diagnosed after 60 is closer to average risk. Ask the age. Do not guess it.
miss: A stool kit at 45 for a patient whose father had colon cancer at 48.
diagramAlt: Positive stool test. Colonoscopy next, not another card Average risk starts at 45 Iron deficiency is diagnostic, not screening

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The recommendation applies to adults with no personal diagnosis or family history of known genetic disorders that predispose them to a high lifetime risk of colorectal cancer, such as Lynch syndrome or familial adenomatous polyposis.

title: Do not order supplemental ultrasound for dense breasts as a proven add-on
lead: The USPSTF does not recommend supplemental ultrasound or MRI for dense breasts on an otherwise negative mammogram. Do not order it as if it were required.
lines: Density is discussed. It is not an automatic second test.
A lump is still imaged diagnostically.
The biennial mammogram remains the screening order.
Biennial mammography from 40 through 74. A palpable mass is diagnostic imaging now, not the next screening date.
Age 75 and older is an individual decision. Supplemental ultrasound for density is not a required add-on.
miss: An automatic breast ultrasound every year because the report said dense.
diagramAlt: Lump versus screen. A mass is diagnostic imaging now Screen: every other year, 40 through 74 Age 75+: not an automatic order

source.name: USPSTF. Breast Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF concludes that the current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of supplemental screening for breast cancer using breast ultrasonography or MRI in women identified to have dense breasts on an otherwise negative screening mammogram.

title: A depression screen without a follow-up slot is an incomplete order
lead: If you screen for depression, the order includes a way to diagnose and treat this week. A form in the chart with no visit is not the USPSTF recommendation.
lines: Pregnancy and the postpartum months are included.
A positive score is an interview, not a prescription by itself.
A universal suicide questionnaire is not the required screen.
Screening is recommended only when systems exist to diagnose and treat. An unread form does not meet that standard.
A stand-alone suicide-risk questionnaire for every adult is an I statement. Ask about suicide when the interview opens that door.
miss: A PHQ-9 in the portal with no one assigned to read it.

source.name: USPSTF. Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF recommends screening for depression in the adult population. To achieve the benefit of depression screening, it is important that persons who screen positive are evaluated further for diagnosis and, if appropriate, are provided or referred for evidence-based care.

title: Do not build a quality metric out of a universal suicide screen
lead: Do not order a stand-alone suicide-risk questionnaire on every adult as a population screen. The USPSTF grade is I.
lines: Ask about suicide when the patient or the depression interview opens that door.
That question is care. It is not the same as a required screen.
A positive depression screen still gets an interview.
Screen adults, including pregnant and postpartum patients, only if someone will diagnose and treat. A positive score is an interview, not an automatic prescription.
The task force found insufficient evidence for stand-alone suicide-risk screening in all adults.
miss: A required suicide score on every annual visit with no depression question.

source.name: USPSTF. Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF concludes that the current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening for suicide risk in the adult population, including pregnant and postpartum persons, as well as older adults.

title: Write the absolute numbers in the after-visit summary
lead: When you recommend a preventive drug or a screen, the after-visit summary states the absolute benefit, not only a relative percentage.
lines: A 50% relative reduction of a rare event can be one in a thousand.
The harm, including false positives, is in the same sentence.
A patient who would decline the next step is not screened.
Shared decision-making uses absolute benefits and harms. Relative reductions alone are misleading.
Write the absolute benefit and the harm in the after-visit summary. A confidence interval that includes no difference is not, by itself, a practice change.
miss: A handout that says cuts your risk in half and gives no baseline.

source.name: USPSTF. Lung Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The decision to undertake screening should involve a discussion of its potential benefits, limitations, and harms. If a person decides to be screened, refer them for lung cancer screening with low-dose CT.

title: Do not order a screening test the patient would not act on
lead: If a patient would not accept a biopsy or a treatment for the disease you might find, do not order the screening test.
lines: Average-risk colorectal screening runs from 45 through 75. Ages 76 to 85 are selective.
A positive stool test is a colonoscopy, not another card.
A patient who would decline colonoscopy and treatment is not started on a screening program.
Bleeding or iron deficiency is a diagnostic colonoscopy, not a screening interval.
miss: Repeating a stool card after a positive test, or screening someone who would refuse the colonoscopy.

source.name: USPSTF. Colorectal Cancer: Screening.
source.says: The USPSTF expanded the recommended ages for colorectal cancer screening to 45 to 75 years. Positive results on stool-based screening tests require follow-up with colonoscopy for the screening benefits to be achieved.

title: Two positive-required tests will miss more people
lead: If you order two tests and require both to be positive before you act, tell the patient you will miss more disease. That structure raises specificity.
lines: Either-positive testing does the opposite.
Write which structure you intended so the next clinician does not mix them.
A single very sensitive test is a different order.
miss: Requiring both a sensitive and a specific test to be positive and thinking you lost no cases.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Sensitivity and specificity are inversely related: as sensitivity increases, specificity tends to decrease, and vice versa. Sensitivity and specificity should always merit consideration together.

title: Either-positive tests need a false-alarm plan
lead: If either of two tests being positive will trigger a biopsy, order the biopsy capacity before you order the pair. Parallel testing creates more false alarms.
lines: The patient is told that more alarms are the price of fewer misses.
Do not add the second test without a plan for the positive.
A pretest probability still comes first.
Parallel testing, where either positive counts, raises sensitivity and lowers specificity. You miss less and alarm more.
miss: Ordering every available test and a promise that a positive means the disease.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Sensitivity and specificity are inversely related: as sensitivity increases, specificity tends to decrease, and vice versa. Sensitivity does not allow providers to understand individuals who tested positive but did not have the disease.

title: A lower cutoff is an order you defend
lead: If you lower a test's cutoff to miss fewer cases, write why, because you will label more healthy people as sick.
lines: You cannot have both perfect sensitivity and perfect specificity at one number.
The lab's reference range is the default unless you document a reason.
A cutoff copied from another population is not automatically yours.
miss: Lowering a cutoff and telling patients the test became more accurate in every way.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Sensitivity and specificity are inversely related: as sensitivity increases, specificity tends to decrease, and vice versa. False positives are a consideration when evaluating specificity and PPV.

title: Do not quote a predictive value from a different population
lead: The positive predictive value you read in a paper does not transfer to your clinic if the disease is rarer here. Recalculate or do not quote it.
lines: Sensitivity can transfer. The predictive value cannot, without the local prevalence.
A screening fair and an emergency department do not share a predictive value.
Write the prevalence you assumed.
miss: Telling a low-risk patient the positive predictive value from a specialty-clinic study.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: Disease prevalence in a population affects PPV and NPV. Providers should consider the sample when reviewing research that reports these values and recognize that the values in their population may differ. Likelihood ratios, like sensitivity and specificity, are not affected by disease prevalence.

title: Write the pre-test chance before you order a rare-disease test
lead: Before you order a test for a rare disease, write the chance you believe the patient has it. A positive result will often be false if that chance is tiny.
lines: Sensitivity does not rescue a near-zero pre-test chance.
The likelihood ratio then revises the number you wrote.
If you cannot name a pre-test chance, you are not ready to interpret the result.
miss: Ordering a rare-disease panel because it is on the menu, with no estimate of the chance.

source.name: StatPearls. Diagnostic Testing Accuracy: Sensitivity, Specificity, Predictive Values and Likelihood Ratios.
source.says: To make clinical decisions and guide patient care, providers must understand the likelihood that a patient has a disease, integrating pretest probability with diagnostic test results. Likelihood ratios allow providers to determine how much a particular test changes the probability.

title: The handoff note names severity in one line
lead: The written handoff starts with illness severity in words the night clinician can use. A list of problems without severity is not a handoff.
lines: The action list is timed: tonight, not soon.
The receiver's read-back is part of the verbal handoff even when the note exists.
A contingency, what to do if the pressure falls, is one sentence.
Illness severity, patient summary, action list with a time, a contingency, and the receiver saying the plan back.
A copied problem list with no watch item is not a handoff. The verbal read-back still happens when a note exists.
miss: A copied problem list with no watch item.
diagramAlt: I-PASS. Illness severity Summary, action list, contingency Receiver says the plan back

source.name: Starmer AJ et al. Changes in medical errors after implementation of a handoff program (I-PASS). N Engl J Med.
source.says: The intervention included a mnemonic to standardize oral and written handoffs and handoff and communication training. The medical-error rate decreased by 23% (24.5 vs. 18.8 per 100 admissions), and preventable adverse events decreased by 30% (4.7 vs. 3.3 per 100 admissions).

title: An opioid agreement is not a reason to abandon the patient
lead: If you stop an opioid, you still treat the pain and the withdrawal. Stopping the prescription is not the end of the relationship.
lines: Naloxone stays on the list if the risk remains.
A benzodiazepine combination is addressed directly.
Ending a relationship requires notice and a way for care to continue. A disagreement about one drug is not abandonment.
Walking away during an emergency is abandonment. A capable refusal of one treatment does not end the rest of care.
miss: Dismissing a patient from the clinic the day you stop the opioid, with no taper and no follow-up.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 1.1.3, Patient Rights.
source.says: A patient with decision-making capacity may accept or refuse any recommended intervention, and patients should expect that their physician will not discontinue treating them when further treatment is medically indicated without notice and reasonable help arranging other care.

more.name: CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain, United States, 2022.

title: Document the interpreter's name in the consent note
lead: The consent note names the professional interpreter. A family member in that blank is an incomplete consent.
lines: The language is recorded.
Questions the patient asked are in the note.
A short interpreter encounter is rescheduled if the procedure is elective and the discussion was rushed.
Consent is disclosure, understanding, and a voluntary choice. The form is the record.
Use a professional interpreter. A child is not the interpreter. The clinician who performs the procedure obtains the consent.

source.name: 45 CFR 92.201. Meaningful access for individuals with limited English proficiency (Section 1557 rule).
source.says: When interpretation is required, a covered entity must offer a qualified interpreter. It must not rely on an adult who is not a qualified interpreter, or on a minor child, to interpret, except as a temporary measure in an emergency while a qualified interpreter is found.

more.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.1, Informed Consent.

title: Write the chaperone's name or the patient's decline

lines: The exam stops if consent is withdrawn.
Each step is explained first.
A declined chaperone is not the same as an offer that was never made.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 1.2.4, Use of Chaperones.
source.says: Physicians should adopt a policy that patients are free to request a chaperone, always honor a request for one, explain the components of the examination, and in general use a chaperone even when a trusted companion is present.

title: A DNR order does not discontinue the antibiotics
lead: If the order is do not resuscitate, the antibiotic, the surgery, and the pain medicine stay unless a separate order stops them.
lines: DNR means no chest compressions and no rescue shocks if the heart stops.
Antibiotics, surgery, dialysis, and opioids are separate orders. A DNR box does not stop them.
Comfort medication is still ordered. Pain is treated whether or not resuscitation is.
Write each limit in words the next shift cannot misread. Ask which treatments the patient still wants.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 5.4, Orders Not to Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR).
source.says: DNAR orders direct the team to withhold resuscitative measures in accord with the patient’s wishes. They apply only to resuscitative interventions; other medically appropriate interventions, such as antibiotics, dialysis, or symptom management, are provided or withheld according to the patient’s wishes.

title: Comfort medicines are ordered before the ventilator is stopped
lead: Before a ventilator is withdrawn, order the opioid or benzodiazepine that will treat air hunger. The withdrawal order and the comfort order are written together.
lines: The intent, relief, is in the note.
A dose chosen to relieve symptoms is not an order to end life.
The family is told what they will see.
Order an opioid for air hunger before the ventilator is withdrawn. The dose is the dose that relieves the symptom.
miss: Stopping the ventilator with no medication for air hunger.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 5.3, Withholding or Withdrawing Life-Sustaining Treatment.
source.says: There is no ethical difference between withholding and withdrawing treatment. When an intervention no longer helps achieve the patient’s goals for care or desired quality of life, it is ethically appropriate to withdraw it.

more.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 5.6, Sedation to Unconsciousness in End-of-Life Care.

title: Put the blood-refusal on the chart before the incision
lead: A capable patient's refusal of blood is a signed order visible to the anesthesiologist and the blood bank before the operation starts.
lines: The consequence, including death, is in the note.
A surrogate does not create a refusal the patient did not make.
A child is transfused if transfusion is life-saving, even if a parent refuses.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 1.1.3, Patient Rights.
source.says: Patients have the right to make decisions about the care the physician recommends and to have those decisions respected. A patient who has decision-making capacity may accept or refuse any recommended medical intervention.

title: Emergency treatment of a child is ordered when a parent refuses
lead: If a parent refuses emergency care that would prevent a child's death or serious harm, order the treatment and notify the protective system.
lines: Explain once, clearly.
Do not delay a life-saving transfusion for a prolonged debate.
Elective care is not this rule.
A life-saving transfusion or emergency operation for a child proceeds when delay would cause death or serious harm. Notify child protection.
Explain once, then treat. Elective care is a different rule: a parent can decline a non-urgent procedure.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.2.1, Pediatric Decision Making.
source.says: Parents or guardians are expected to safeguard their children’s physical health and well-being when giving or withholding permission for treatment. Except when immediate intervention is essential to preserve life or avert serious, irreversible harm, a child’s refusal should be respected; ongoing disagreement goes to an ethics committee.

more.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 8.10, Preventing, Identifying and Treating Violence and Abuse.

title: A cesarean refusal is documented, and the patient is not taken against it
lead: If a capable patient refuses a cesarean, document the fetal risk you explained and do not write an order to proceed.

Continue other care that the patient accepts. A refusal of one operation is not a refusal of monitoring or of antibiotics.
Do not obtain a new signature after a sedative. Capacity for this decision is judged before the drug.
miss: Writing an operative order after a capable patient has refused the cesarean.

title: Sterilization is not added to a cesarean consent in labor
lead: Do not add tubal ligation to a cesarean consent signed during labor unless a considered consent was obtained before labor.
lines: Pain and fear make that moment inadequate.
A prior antenatal consent is confirmed, not assumed.
The cesarean itself still needs its own current consent.
Consent for sterilization is obtained before labor, when deliberation is possible. A signature between contractions is not adequate.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.1, Informed Consent.
source.says: In seeking informed consent, physicians should assess the patient’s ability to understand relevant medical information and the implications of alternatives and to make an independent, voluntary decision.

title: Implied consent is a note that says why you could not wait
lead: When you treat an emergency without consent, the note says what the emergency was, whom you tried to reach, and why delay was unsafe.
lines: If delay would cause serious harm and no surrogate can be reached, treat.
That note does not cover an elective addition.
Keep looking for the surrogate while you treat. Write the note at the time.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.1, Informed Consent.
source.says: In emergencies, when a decision must be made urgently, the patient cannot participate, and the surrogate is not available, physicians may initiate treatment without prior informed consent, then inform the patient or surrogate at the earliest opportunity and obtain consent for ongoing treatment.

title: Recheck capacity when the sodium or the drug wears off
lead: A capacity determination is redone when the sodium, the oxygen, or the sedative changes. Do not leave a one-time note as a permanent label.
lines: The question is this decision, today.
A refusal that appears after the patient clears may be valid.
The earlier note is not deleted. An addendum says what changed.
Understand, appreciate, reason, and express a choice, for this decision, today. It can return when sodium, oxygen, or a sedative changes.
Disagreement with the recommendation is not incapacity. Competence is the court's word.

source.name: StatPearls. Competency and Capacity.
source.says: Capacity is a functional determination that an individual is or is not capable of making a medical decision within a given situation, relative to baseline and pertaining only to the current situation. Competence is a legal determination made by a judge, never by medical providers.

more.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.2, Decisions for Adult Patients Who Lack Capacity.

title: An against-advice departure still gets the prescription that makes leaving safer
lead: If a capable patient leaves against advice, order the antibiotic or the insulin they need for a safer exit, and document the risks you explained.
lines: A signature is ideal and is not required for the note to count.
Offer to treat the dangerous problem before they go.
Capacity for this decision is one line in the note.
A capable patient may leave. Offer the antibiotic or insulin that makes leaving safer. Do not withhold it as a punishment.
Document the risks and the capacity assessment even if the patient will not sign.

title: A POLST is placed where emergency clinicians will see it
lead: A completed POLST is copied to the record and the patient is told to keep it where ambulance crews look. An advance directive in a lawyer's office does not travel.
lines: A POLST is a medical order that emergency clinicians can follow. An advance directive guides a surrogate and is not itself a field order.
Put the POLST where the ambulance and the emergency department will see it. A form left in a drawer does not travel.
A capable patient can void it. Reconcile a full-code note and a DNR order before discharge so they do not contradict.

lines: Photograph and document injuries in words a later reader can see.
Treat the injury.
Do not promise the family you will keep it between you.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 8.10, Preventing, Identifying and Treating Violence and Abuse.
source.says: Physicians should treat the immediate symptoms and sequelae of violence and abuse and report suspected violence and abuse in keeping with applicable requirements.

title: Remove an impaired colleague from patients before the report is finished
lead: If a colleague is impaired now, they stop seeing patients immediately. The report follows. It does not come first while they keep working.
lines: A suspicion you cannot yet support is reported through the proper channel, not announced in the hallway.
Your discomfort is not a reason to wait.

Review patients already seen. A hallway announcement is not the reporting channel.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 9.3.2, Physician Responsibilities to Colleagues with Illness, Disability or Impairment.
source.says: Physicians should intervene with respect and compassion when a colleague is not able to practice safely, ensure the colleague no longer endangers patients, and promote appropriate interventions, seeking assistance in keeping with institutional policies, regulatory requirements, or law.

title: An addendum after a complication is timed and signed
lead: After a complication, corrections are an addendum with the time you learned the fact. Do not reopen and rewrite the original note.
lines: The disclosure to the patient matches the addendum.
A late entry is labeled late.
Deleting a line is not an option the record allows honestly.

source.name: AMA Principles of Medical Ethics, Principle II.
source.says: A physician shall uphold the standards of professionalism, be honest in all professional interactions, and strive to report physicians deficient in character or competence, or engaging in fraud or deception, to appropriate entities.

title: Research procedures are a separate consent form
lead: A research biopsy or an extra vial is a separate consent. It is not added to the clinical consent the morning of surgery.
lines: The patient can refuse and still have the operation.
The form says what is experimental.
The person obtaining research consent can explain the study.
A research biopsy needs its own consent that explains the study, the alternatives, and the right to refuse without losing standard care.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 7.1.2, Informed Consent in Research.
source.says: Physicians must ensure voluntary, informed consent before enrolling a participant in research, disclosing the nature of the research, its risks, and that alternatives are open, including standard or no treatment instead of participating.

title: Do not order a placebo disguised as a drug
lead: Do not order a placebo labeled as an active pain medicine. If a symptom needs treatment, order a real treatment or an honest explanation.
lines: The patient who improves on a real explanation does not need a deception.
Trust is part of the next visit.
Labeling a sugar capsule as an active analgesic is deception. It is not a therapeutic trial.
A research placebo requires a consent that says it is a placebo. Symptoms still get a real evaluation.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 2.1.4, Use of Placebo in Clinical Practice.
source.says: Using a placebo without the patient’s knowledge may undermine trust and harm the patient. Physicians may use placebos only if they enlist the patient’s cooperation and obtain the patient’s general consent to administer a placebo.

title: Call the designated requester for organ donation
lead: When death is near and donation is possible, call the designated requester. Do not tie your recommendation to stop support to a yes on donation.
lines: The withdrawal decision is documented on its own.
The family is not told that stopping depends on agreeing to donation.
Your role and the requester's role stay separate.

Do not offer to stop the ventilator only if the family agrees to donation.

source.name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics. Opinion 6.1.2, Organ Donation After Cardiac Death.
source.says: Ensure that the decision to withdraw life-sustaining treatment is made prior to and independent of any offer of opportunity to donate organs, unless the patient or surrogate raises donation, and that no member of the transplant team has a role in the decision to withdraw treatment.
